An attacker varying one header pumps unlimited OTP SMS, each a real message the restaurant is billed for. The per-phone limit the code's own comment calls what stops a brute force is the only control left standing.

nodes.label: cod-conversion-leaves-upi-link-payable (MEDIUM, confirmed)
nodes.rationale: Same class as the M1 review's resend finding, reached through a different door and missed by that fix, and it cannot be fixed the same way because markPaid honours a superseded unpaid link on purpose. Detection matters as well as prevention: moving the order to needs_attention would throw inside markPaid's transaction and make the gateway retry forever, so an explicit refund-due signal is preferred.

nodes.label: session-role-never-rechecked-against-the-row (MEDIUM, confirmed)
nodes.rationale: An agent who leaves or a staff member the owner removes keeps full access for up to seven days from any device where the cookie was already set, including the admin-only audit log showing every restaurant's write history; an owner demoted to staff keeps owner-only powers until the cookie expires. There is no way for anyone to cut a session short.

nodes.label: convert-to-cod-leaves-upi-link-payable (LOW, confirmed)
nodes.rationale: The third independent account of the same class. attachPayment supersedes outstanding awaiting rows — that was the M1 review fix for the resend path — but the convert-to-COD path, which exists precisely because the customer did not pay the UPI link, was not covered by it. The exact failure the M1 fix was written to close, reached through a different door.

nodes.label: empty-assistant-turn-after-round-cap (LOW, confirmed)
nodes.rationale: Hitting the tool-round cap pushes an assistant turn with null text into the session and keeps it for the rest of the call. Gemini tolerates it, checked against the live key, so the primary provider is fine; Anthropic rejects a non-final message with empty content, so the Build Spec §3 failover would 400 on every subsequent turn — four strikes and a vendor_error transfer for a call that was otherwise healthy. Explicitly recorded as NOT REPRODUCED against Anthropic because no key exists. Fix: keep the assistant turn and give it the line the caller actually hears.

nodes.label: orders-today-never-resets-at-midnight (LOW, confirmed)
nodes.rationale: A counter tablet left on overnight carries yesterday's total into today, so just after midnight the board says 27 orders today when today has one. The number is the design's reassurance figure, so it quietly misreports the day's trade until someone reloads. Fix with a timer on the IST day the count belongs to, not a refresh.

nodes.label: duplicate-saved-addresses (LOW, confirmed)
nodes.rationale: A regular customer's saved-address list fills with identical entries they cannot delete; on a slow connection a single double-tap does it in one order. Build Spec §6 puts saved addresses first precisely so a repeat customer taps once. Normalisation must handle case and internal whitespace, and lastUsedAt must not be bumped on a mere re-save or a retyped address would outrank one the customer actually ordered to.

nodes.label: nag-drops-a-missed-week (refuted)
nodes.rationale: Refuted as a nag bug: one week at a time is the decided behaviour in the design, it satisfies the Build Spec §14 acceptance that the prompt persists until answered, and the existing test deliberately asserts it.

nodes.label: billing-page-hardcodes-zero-ai-calls (refuted)
nodes.rationale: Refuted: countAllowanceCalls filters transport = exotel by documented decision and nothing at M2 can create an Exotel call, since the only session-init route pins transport to browser. The claimed consequence requires call rows nothing in the repo can write, and the page copy already labels the figure as from M2.

nodes.label: stale-open-orders-silence-monday-nag-forever (refuted)
nodes.rationale: Refuted: rushCount's lack of a time bound implements the design word for word — three or more active orders, not today's orders — and the existing test deliberately asserts the boundary.

nodes.label: orderNumbers (src/db/repos/dashboard.ts)
nodes.rationale: Buckets orders into IST calendar days with (placed_at + interval '330 minutes')::date. Casting a timestamptz to date uses the database session TimeZone, which PGlite initdb's from the host's UTC offset rounded to whole hours, so the offsets stack. Nothing in the 289-test suite covers it.

nodes.label: convertToCod (src/db/repos/dashboard.ts)
nodes.rationale: Switches an order to cash and resets payment_status to unpaid but leaves every payment row at awaiting and never cancels the gateway link, so markPaid still honours it.

nodes.label: externalOrdersBetween (src/db/repos/dashboard.ts)
nodes.rationale: Sums aggregator counts only for weeks whose Monday falls inside the queried month, which is what makes the Direct Order Share numerator and denominator cover different spans.

nodes.label: externalWeeksBetween (src/db/repos/dashboard.ts)
nodes.rationale: Proposed replacement returning the entered weeks themselves as week_start plus order counts, with the window widened so a week overlapping the month boundary is not silently dropped. Placed in the repo layer rather than the page because app/ holds routes only.

nodes.label: countAllowanceCalls (src/db/repos/dashboard.ts)
nodes.rationale: Filters transport = exotel by documented decision, so it returns 0 for every outlet at M2 — the basis on which the billing-page claim was refuted.

nodes.label: OrderCard (src/ui/OrderCard.tsx)
nodes.rationale: Renders the order number the kitchen shouts across the counter, and the lean-in expand row whose target size and aria-label were design-fidelity findings at M1.

nodes.label: place_order tool handler (src/voice/tools.ts)
nodes.rationale: Calls src/checkout/place-order.ts with an ai_call context. Carried three of the highest-severity findings across two reviews: writing a profile row with no consent check, and having no per-call idempotency guard while never clearing session.cart.

nodes.label: record_consent tool handler (src/voice/tools.ts)
nodes.rationale: Writes a consent_record with channel call and spoken-rendering evidence. Added by ADR 0005 as the fourteenth tool.

nodes.label: search_menu tool handler (src/voice/tools.ts)
nodes.rationale: The structural menu-grounding gate: add_to_cart accepts only ids search_menu returned in this session, so the model supplies ids and quantities and can never invent an item or a price.

nodes.label: add_to_cart tool handler (src/voice/tools.ts)
nodes.rationale: Prices trial additions against session.searchResults rather than the live published menu, which is half of the read-back divergence.

nodes.label: cartSummary (src/voice/tools.ts)
nodes.rationale: Prices the cart against a snapshot taken when search_menu ran, while placeOrder re-prices against the live published menu. Its own comment claims the two cannot diverge, which is the invariant the fix actually establishes. It also calls priceCart uncaught.

nodes.label: use_saved_address tool handler (src/voice/tools.ts)
nodes.rationale: Returned the caller's spoken address line in the tool result, and was bypassable because loop.ts pre-set session.addressId.

nodes.label: runTool (src/voice/tools.ts)
nodes.rationale: Propagates a thrown CartError rather than converting it to a structured refusal, which turns a dish going sold out mid-call into a failed call.

nodes.label: takeTurn (src/voice/loop.ts)
nodes.rationale: One turn: guardrails before the model, the LLM adapter with tool schemas, tool execution, at most four rounds, then the reply and the ledger. The site of the consent ordering bug, the closing short-circuit and the empty assistant turn.

nodes.label: note (src/voice/loop.ts)
nodes.rationale: Records a tool call's effect on the call record. Guarded by closing ??= note(...), whose short-circuit drops bookkeeping for every tool after a closing signal in the same round.

nodes.label: placeOrder (src/checkout/place-order.ts)
nodes.rationale: The single shared checkout path the web page and the voice assistant both call, which is the point of ADR 0004. Carried the refused-code block, the paid-by-UPI SMS wording, the missing confirmation for address-pending orders and the unreturned SMS cost.

nodes.label: issuePaymentLink (src/checkout/place-order.ts)
nodes.rationale: One of the two places that issue a replacement link, and therefore one of the two places that must cancel the previous awaiting link at the gateway first, outside the transaction.

nodes.label: sendOrderConfirm (proposed, src/checkout/place-order.ts)
nodes.rationale: Proposed extraction of the order_confirm send over the existing SmsTarget so the address-confirmation path can call it for every payment method.

nodes.label: priceCart (src/core/cart.ts)
nodes.rationale: Never checks that a line's unit price is at least zero, so a variant or option delta larger than the base price produces a negative line, a negative subtotal and a negative order total; with a discount code the negative subtotal makes applyPercentDiscount throw a RangeError, breaking the documented throws-CartError contract and escaping every caller's catch.

nodes.label: priceLine (src/core/cart.ts)
nodes.rationale: Where the accumulated unit-price guard belongs, after both the variant and the option deltas are applied, since an option delta reaches the same state as a variant delta.

nodes.label: applyPercentDiscount (src/core/cart.ts)
nodes.rationale: Throws a RangeError on a negative subtotal — not a CartError, so it escapes every caller's catch and surfaces to the customer only as Something went wrong.

nodes.label: prune (app/(customer)/r/[slug]/cart.ts)
nodes.rationale: Validates that a saved cart line's item, variant and option ids still exist but not that the line still satisfies each option group's minSelect and maxSelect, so an ordinary menu edit leaves a line that makes priceCart throw. Identified as the single authority that should decide whether a line can still be priced.

nodes.label: attachPayment (src/db/repos/orders.ts)
nodes.rationale: Its own comment claims the link it replaces is closed; nothing closes it, and only the old payment row's status changes in our database. The misleading comment is what makes the defect look fixed on a read-through.

nodes.label: markPaid (src/db/repos/orders.ts)
nodes.rationale: Guards only on the payment row being paid and the order being paid, neither of which a COD conversion sets, and returns alreadyPaid for a second capture without recording it — so a double charge leaves no trace to refund against.

nodes.label: estimateInvoice (src/core/billing.ts)
nodes.rationale: Has no notion of the trial: always adds SUBSCRIPTION_PAISE and always measures overage against CALL_ALLOWANCE, although Build Spec §13 gives a new restaurant 30 days or 150 allowance calls free.

nodes.label: resendPaymentLink (app/(restaurant)/app/(shell)/board-actions.ts)
nodes.rationale: Refuses only when the order is already paid or is not a UPI-link order and never checks status, so the only guard against resending on a cancelled or delivered order is the client's canResendLink.

nodes.label: src/auth/secrets.ts — SESSION_SECRET and PHONE_HASH_PEPPER
nodes.rationale: Fell back to a constant-derived sha256 outside production, a value anyone can compute from the repo, contrary to the repository rule that a missing variable is an error and never a silent fallback.

nodes.label: requirePlatform (src/auth/session.ts)
nodes.rationale: Trusts the role and sub claims in the JWT and never looks the user up; there is no revocation list, so signing out only deletes the cookie on one device.

nodes.label: requireStaff (src/auth/session.ts)
nodes.rationale: Same defect as requirePlatform: a removed counter staff member or a demoted owner keeps their powers for the token's seven-day life.

nodes.label: createSession (src/auth/session.ts)
nodes.rationale: Minted a 30-day customer session from a 7-day bearer token travelling in a URL at the address-confirmation endpoint.

nodes.label: saveAddress (src/db/repos/customers.ts)
nodes.rationale: Always inserts with no uniqueness check on customerId, restaurantId, normalised line1 and pincode, and the form has no disabled-while-pending state. The fix belongs here rather than in the form because the address-link and manual-order callers bypass the form entirely.

nodes.label: upsertItem (src/db/repos/menu.ts)
nodes.rationale: The one choke point both menu parsers pass through — the agent console's itemForm and the restaurant app's menu actions are separate parsers — so the non-negative price guard belongs here rather than only in the forms.

nodes.label: Board (app/(restaurant)/app/(shell)/Board.tsx)
nodes.rationale: todayCount is seeded once server-side and thereafter only incremented by merge; nothing re-renders the board at the IST day boundary, and a counter tablet left on overnight is what a counter tablet does.

nodes.label: MondayNag (app/(restaurant)/app/(shell)/MondayNag.tsx)
nodes.rationale: The quick-pick chips wrote fabricated midpoints into external_order_count, so a restaurant doing 300 aggregator orders a week recorded 75 and the North Star was overstated several-fold as if it were exact.

nodes.label: MenuClient (app/(customer)/r/[slug]/MenuClient.tsx)
nodes.rationale: The ordering page's only client code — cart, stepper, option chooser, about 5 KB gzipped. Swallowed a priceCart throw into cart = null, hiding the cart bar with no error and no way forward.

nodes.label: ConfirmStep (app/(customer)/r/[slug]/checkout/ConfirmStep.tsx)
nodes.rationale: Swallows the same priceCart throw as MenuClient and renders Your cart is empty while the cart is still in localStorage.

nodes.label: placeOrderAction (app/(customer)/r/[slug]/checkout/actions.ts)
nodes.rationale: The web checkout's trust boundary. Originally checked only for a session, not for live order_fulfilment consent; the gate added here is the one the voice channel was then found to be missing.

nodes.label: confirmAddressAction (app/(customer)/r/[slug]/address/[token]/actions.ts)
nodes.rationale: Calls only issuePaymentLink, which returns null for a COD order, so a COD voice delivery order produces exactly one SMS in its whole life — the address link.

nodes.label: setAvailability (app/(restaurant)/app/(shell)/menu/actions.ts)
nodes.rationale: Toggled any menu_item uuid with no check that it belongs to the session's outlet, while item uuids ship to every browser that opens an ordering page.

nodes.label: createRestaurantAction (app/(platform)/agent/restaurants/new/actions.ts)
nodes.rationale: Returned a driver error message verbatim, which for drizzle-orm 0.45 embeds the failing SQL and its parameters.

nodes.label: lookupCustomer (app/(restaurant)/app/(shell)/orders/new/actions.ts)
nodes.rationale: Returned found:true from the platform-wide customer table before the restaurant-scoped consent check, letting any staff login test whether a phone has ever used any ServeLine restaurant.

nodes.label: cancelLink (src/adapters/payments)
nodes.rationale: The missing adapter method behind five separate double-charge findings. Cancelling at the gateway is what actually closes the hole; marking rows unpaid in our database does not stop a capture. Must be called before the replacement link is created, outside the transaction, and must tolerate failure because a link already captured cannot be cancelled and that must not fail a resend.

nodes.label: toAnthropicMessages (src/adapters/llm/anthropic.ts)
nodes.rationale: Maps an empty assistant turn to content: [], which Anthropic rejects for a non-final message — so a call that once hit the round cap would fail over into a provider that 400s on every subsequent turn.

nodes.label: weekToAsk (src/core/aggregator-nag.ts)
nodes.rationale: One week at a time is the decided behaviour, with a real Skip and four weeks of silence after three skips; the test deliberately asserts it. The basis on which the missed-week claim was refuted.

nodes.label: rushCount (src/core/aggregator-nag.ts)
nodes.rationale: Its lack of a time bound implements the design's rush rule word for word — three or more active orders, not today's orders — and the existing test deliberately asserts the boundary. The basis on which the stale-open-orders claim was refuted.

nodes.label: appendTurn (src/db/repos/calls.ts)
nodes.rationale: Stores call_turn.text unsanitised, so a spoken phone number lands on a fifth table outside the four the repository rules allow.

nodes.label: client IP helper (proposed, src/auth/client-ip.ts)
nodes.rationale: One helper every call site uses instead of inlining the header split, trusting only what the deployment controls rather than a client-supplied X-Forwarded-For element.

nodes.label: Steel & Enamel — the direction
nodes.rationale: The surface is a working steel counter; state arrives as flat enamel plates fixed to it. Steel is ServeLine's and never changes; enamel belongs to the order or to the restaurant. Drawn from the material world of an Indian restaurant counter — stainless steel, cool and unsentimental, carrying vitreous enamel signage that survives grease, heat and twenty years of hands. Honest risk: a cool steel-grey system can read as cold to an owner expecting something that looks like an app, mitigated by the enamel edge and the restaurant's own colour in the header.

nodes.label: Two layers, and they never mix
nodes.rationale: Steel carries no meaning; state enamel belongs to the order lifecycle; house enamel belongs to the restaurant. Because state enamel and house enamel never occupy the same component, a restaurant whose brand colour is exactly the received blue causes no collision — there is nothing to collide with. This resolves the hardest problem in the brief as a side effect.
nodes.norm_label: two layers, and they never mix

nodes.label: Colour is never a button
nodes.rationale: The primary action is a filled steel-900 plate with white text at 16.16:1 everywhere except the customer surface, where the restaurant's own colour takes it. On the counter dashboard zero chroma competes with state. Described as the most load-bearing decision in the document.

nodes.label: Plates, not pills
nodes.rationale: Status chips are 4px-radius rectangles, not 999px capsules. A rectangle holds a long Kannada string at the same height a capsule holds a short English one, and it reads as stamped hardware rather than a consumer app tag. Pills are also the consumer-marketplace tell and waste horizontal space long Kannada strings need.

nodes.label: Delivered returns to steel
nodes.rationale: Terminal states are drained, not recoloured, so a board of completed orders is grey and quiet. Only three of six states — received, ready, needs-attention — are permitted to be chromatically loud.

nodes.label: The steel neutral ramp
nodes.rationale: Cool, low-chroma and blue-green-shifted: not a pure grey, which is the digital default, and emphatically not warm, since cream is the rendition trap this brief invites. Dark-mode roles deliberately do not mirror the light ramp — steel-500 is a legal body colour on light at 4.69 but fails on dark at 3.86, so ramp steps must never be paired by number.

nodes.label: State enamel — six states, four tokens each
nodes.rationale: ink for text, icons and the 4px card edge; plate for the filled chip; on for text on plate; wash for a tint ground. Every pair passes AA at 4.5:1 with zero failures across 24 measured pairs. Card state edges always use ink, never plate.
nodes.norm_label: state enamel — six states, four tokens each

nodes.label: Palette law — a hue is reserved for exactly one meaning
nodes.rationale: The six state hues may not appear as decoration, illustration, chart fill, marketing accent or hover tint anywhere in the product. If another colour is needed for something that is not an order state, it may not be had — use steel. Donated from a declined arcade-pixel challenger world.
nodes.norm_label: palette law — a hue is reserved for exactly one meaning

nodes.label: Anti-aggregator, verified numerically
nodes.rationale: The amber and the red were moved until the ΔE-OK arithmetic cleared against Swiggy and Zomato chrome. preparing became brass — 30.6° of hue separation from Swiggy and materially correct, since steel plus brass plus enamel is the actual hardware palette of an Indian commercial kitchen. needs-attention became oxblood and is honestly recorded at ΔE-OK 0.099 from Zomato's darker red, marginally under threshold, made safe by two rules rather than hopes: the darker ink carries the majority of usage, and red is never a field.

nodes.label: Never colour alone — three redundant encodings
nodes.rationale: Every state carries an edge (position plus colour), a glyph (shape) and a translated text label. The glyph set is script-neutral and ordinal — the first three are a 3-segment progress bar, legible in monochrome and to a viewer who reads none of the three languages. Shipped as inline SVG of about 80 bytes each, not an icon font and not an emoji.
nodes.norm_label: never colour alone — three redundant encodings

nodes.label: The restaurant brand colour normalizer
nodes.rationale: A raw brand hex never reaches the DOM. A deterministic OKLCH normalizer runs at onboarding-save time, preserving hue always and constraining only lightness and chroma so the restaurant still recognises its colour, then the derived tokens are shipped as a small inline style block keyed by slug. Tested against twelve hostile inputs with zero AA failures; pure white and pure black both normalise to neutral grey, which is correct because an achromatic brand has no hue to preserve. Computing OKLCH in the client would be JS budget spent on arithmetic doable once at save time.

nodes.label: Where brand colour may appear — a deliberately short list
nodes.rationale: Customer page: header band, primary CTA, active category tab underline, selected-row wash, logo chip. Dashboard: a 4px identity rail and the wordmark, and nothing else, because the board is a state instrument. Agent console: a swatch preview in the config field only. The page must be complete and handsome with no brand at all, which is the day-one state of every restaurant.
nodes.norm_label: where brand colour may appear — a deliberately short list

nodes.label: Zero webfonts, product-wide
nodes.rationale: One weight across three scripts is roughly 175-250 KB — 1.75x to 2.5x the entire JS budget in fonts alone — and subsetting does not rescue it, because Indic text is unbounded user content and a dish added tomorrow with an unsubsetted conjunct renders as tofu. font-display:swap is not free either, since fallback and webfont metrics differ far more across scripts than within Latin, producing a visible multi-line reflow mid-menu. Two consequences stated plainly: ServeLine's identity cannot live in a typeface, and the cross-script mismatch is accepted rather than papered over.

nodes.label: The trilingual system font stack
nodes.rationale: CSS font matching is per character, not per string, so Latin UI faces sit first and Devanagari and Kannada characters fall through to the first family covering them — Nirmala UI on Windows, Kohinoor and Kannada Sangam MN on macOS, Noto Sans Devanagari and Kannada on Android and Linux where they are already part of the system set. On the target handsets all three scripts render with zero font bytes downloaded.

nodes.label: Indic typography rules
nodes.rationale: Weights 400 and 700 only for any string that can be Indic, because low-end Android system Indic faces commonly ship Regular and Bold only and 500/600 get synthesised unpredictably. Never clamp Indic text with a pixel max-height or a line-height below 1.45, or matras and below-base forms get clipped.

nodes.label: Motion budget — transform and opacity only
nodes.rationale: Nothing exceeds 300ms because users are in a task. Banned on the customer surface and the counter phone: layout-triggering properties, box-shadow and filter and backdrop-filter, skeleton shimmer (use a static steel-100 block on a battery device propped at a counter all day), FLIP list reorder, page transitions and parallax, more than two concurrently animating elements, and any infinite iteration count bar one exception.
nodes.norm_label: motion budget — transform and opacity only

nodes.label: The new-order alert — the one hard motion problem
nodes.rationale: A loud kitchen, a propped phone, a glancing operator: motion alone will not do it and an infinite pulse is the wrong answer because it drains battery and the eye habituates within a day. Sound first — a two-tone chime, user-testable, disableable, unlocked by a gesture. Then a persistent static high-contrast band that says how many and stays until acknowledged. Exactly three attention cycles, then still: three cycles catch a glance, infinity trains the eye to ignore it. A count, not a re-sort. Under reduced motion the pulse does not run and nothing is lost, because the alert never depends on motion for its meaning.
nodes.norm_label: the new-order alert — the one hard motion problem

nodes.label: Reduced motion and flatten-and-pose
nodes.rationale: A global reduce block, then intent restored selectively: opacity-only cross-fades at ≤100ms permitted, transforms not. Replace a continuous animation with a two-state before/after swap, never with a slower version of the same animation. Donated from a declined tensegrity-force world.

nodes.label: The accessibility floor
nodes.rationale: The order board is a list of articles, not a table, because a table forces cell-by-cell reading and a TalkBack operator needs one order announced as one unit. Exactly two live regions, and only one assertive region product-wide, reserved for new-order arrival. lang on any element whose content differs from the page. The language switcher is a real labelled select and never a flag icon, because a flag is a country, not a language. Every input has a persistent visible label, since a placeholder-only field is unusable for a low-tech-comfort user who taps in and loses the prompt. Zoom is never disabled.

nodes.label: The dual-tone focus ring
nodes.rationale: The ring can land on top of a restaurant's arbitrary brand colour, so it cannot itself be a colour. Two concentric shadows, one of which always contrasts — verified at 4.9:1 and 3.3:1 against a normalised mid-blue brand fill. Never remove the ring, never rely on :focus without :focus-visible, and keep the sticky cart bar and alert band from obscuring a focused element.

nodes.label: The Monday aggregator-count nag
nodes.rationale: Once per week, Monday, first dashboard open, collecting the two numbers behind the North Star. Skip this week must not be hard to find, because that is a dark pattern and it poisons the very metric being collected, and the nag is deferred during a rush of three or more active orders.

nodes.label: The copy-pasteable token set
nodes.rationale: The whole system as CSS custom properties, which is what src/ui consumes; components never hard-code a colour or a spacing value.

nodes.label: Contrast gates to enforce in CI (design §13)
nodes.norm_label: contrast gates to enforce in ci (design §13)

nodes.label: Fixed board positions — the board never re-sorts
nodes.rationale: An order's position is stable for its whole life so the operator's eye learns where things are; new arrivals are announced by a counter at the top, never by pushing the board around under a moving finger. Kept from the rejected Departure Board direction.
nodes.norm_label: fixed board positions — the board never re-sorts

nodes.label: Seams, not shadows, and isolated destruction
nodes.rationale: Panel division is a 1px border because soft shadows band visibly on cheap LCD panels and cost compositing on a phone already thermally throttled. Cancel order is never adjacent to Mark ready. Kept from the rejected Dark Developer Console direction.
nodes.norm_label: seams, not shadows, and isolated destruction

nodes.label: Rejected direction — Kitchen Ticket
nodes.rationale: The author's own top-ranked candidate, rejected because it is the single most obvious artefact of the category, renders as cream paper plus monospace, and is literally what the aggregator's tablet prints — so it would make ServeLine look like aggregator plumbing rather than the restaurant's own tool. Mono figures also fail: no monospace face on a cheap Android covers all three scripts. Kept from it: tabular figures, and one order as one bounded object with a hard edge.

nodes.label: Rejected direction — Departure Board
nodes.rationale: Wins audience identification and loses product clarity: a one-surface idea whose per-character cascade motion grammar is unaffordable on a cheap Android and banned outright on 3G. Kept from it: fixed positions.

nodes.label: Rejected direction — Dark Developer Console
nodes.rationale: Wins product clarity on the agent console and loses audience identification on the two surfaces that matter more — a graphite console reads not-for-me to a diner and to a fifty-five-year-old restaurant owner, and it is the tool-monoculture default the direction roll exists to refuse. Kept from it: seams not shadows, and isolated destruction.

nodes.label: Rejected direction — Orienteering Legend
nodes.rationale: Rejected because orienteering is not a literacy this audience has. Donated the course-never-edits-the-terrain idea, which became the two-layer rule and is the cleanest answer to how a brand colour slots in safely, plus legend discipline — every mark defined in one ranked table, which is what a trilingual low-tech-comfort audience needs.

nodes.label: Six open decisions a builder must not invent
nodes.rationale: Accessibility standard, stack, dark-mode entry point, Hindi and Kannada state vocabulary, alert sound, and whether delivered and completed are one state or two. The research declined to invent them; ADR 0002 settles four and records two as pending with an interim.
nodes.norm_label: six open decisions a builder must not invent

nodes.label: Performance notes that are design decisions
nodes.rationale: Zero webfonts, images off by default on the menu, no shadows on the customer surface, static loading blocks instead of shimmer, inline SVG glyphs rather than an icon font, and outline chips on the customer surface. These belong in the design document because they constrain the visual system, not just the build.
nodes.norm_label: performance notes that are design decisions

nodes.label: Steel & Enamel — ServeLine design language
nodes.rationale: Research and direction document written from the brief alone with no interactive answer channel, so its inferences are marked and its §14 lists six decisions a builder must not invent. Every colour pair was computed rather than estimated (WCAG relative luminance, OKLCH, ΔE-OK) and §13 describes the script that reproduces them.

nodes.label: M1 review — 20 September 2026
nodes.rationale: Two independent review passes over commit 2dd4531, run after every Build Spec §14 M1 acceptance criterion had already passed in a browser. Spec-fidelity and security: 2 high, 7 medium, 5 low. Design fidelity against the Steel & Enamel contract: 0 high, 3 medium, 8 low. Three findings were not acted on with reasons recorded.

nodes.label: M2 review — 21 September 2026
nodes.rationale: Two independent review passes over commit c52bb87, after the M2 design's acceptance criteria had passed against the scripted mock. Ten spec/security findings (2 high) and nine design-fidelity findings. Two were not acted on. The review is the origin of ADR 0005: its HIGH finding that place_order wrote a profile row without consent forced the gate that then required a spoken-consent tool.

nodes.label: Bug hunt — 22 September 2026
nodes.rationale: Six hunters over every layer of the platform, each finding then handed to an independent verifier told to refute it. Reproduction was required — a bug nobody could trigger was dropped. 27 claims verified, 24 confirmed, 3 refuted. Several bugs were found independently by more than one hunter and appear once under the clearest account.

nodes.label: ServeLine M1 — design
nodes.rationale: Agreed 18 Sep 2026 for Build Spec §14 milestone M1, orders without AI. Product decisions are not made here; where it disagrees with Ideation, Ideation wins. M1 is where the shape of everything after it is set — the order state machine, the consent record, the cart and the code-redemption rules are built as pure functions precisely so the voice service reuses them unchanged at M2.

nodes.label: ServeLine M2 — design
nodes.rationale: Agreed 20 Sep 2026 for milestone M2, the voice service built without a telephone line or speech vendor. Builds the assistant's brain plus two vendor-free transports (browser mic, agent-console simulator). The same-as-last-time shortcut is pulled forward from M3 because it is the thirty-second call and the product's signature moment, and costs one tool once the brain exists.

nodes.label: ServeLine — Build Spec
nodes.rationale: The engineering specification every ADR amends or departs from. Sections cited across this chunk: §3 voice orchestration and LLM, §4 data model and order states, §5.2-§5.6 the call contract, §6 the ordering page, §7 the dashboard, §9 SMS, §10 consent and privacy, §12 metrics, §13 billing, §14 milestone acceptance, §15 repository layout, §16 performance and evaluation.

nodes.label: ServeLine — Ideation
nodes.rationale: The product record. Product decisions live here and behaviour not decided here must not be invented. Cited for §6 the win-back loop, §7 the AI call assistant as the wedge, §9 Direct Order Share as the North Star, §10 the per-call cost envelope and allowance, §11 does-not-ship, §15 the consent approach being a legal reading rather than counsel-reviewed.

nodes.label: M1 SEC-1 — phone numbers and addresses escape in driver error messages (high)
nodes.rationale: drizzle-orm 0.45's DrizzleQueryError message embeds the failing SQL and its parameters, so any driver failure — lock, connection drop, constraint race — throws an error whose message contains the phone number or full address, and the server actions let it escape to Next's server-side error log. Fix: catch and rethrow a sanitised error keeping cause.code and constraint while dropping query and params.
nodes.norm_label: m1 sec-1 — phone numbers and addresses escape in driver error messages (high)

nodes.label: M1 SEC-2 — setAvailability toggles any outlet's menu item (high)
nodes.rationale: Item uuids are public — they ship to every browser that opens an ordering page — so a staff login at restaurant A can mark restaurant B's whole menu sold out. The ownership check already exists in the sibling saveItem action.
nodes.norm_label: m1 sec-2 — setavailability toggles any outlet's menu item (high)

nodes.label: M1 SEC-3 — manual order links a customer profile regardless of consent (medium)
nodes.rationale: Violates Build Spec §7's links-the-order-to-a-profile-if-consent-exists and §10, and inflates the §12 profile-capture metric. Keep the phone-only customer row for the UPI link but leave the order unlinked.
nodes.norm_label: m1 sec-3 — manual order links a customer profile regardless of consent (medium)

nodes.label: M1 SEC-4 — placeOrderAction checks only for a session, not for live consent (medium)
nodes.rationale: A customer who withdrew consent with an old checkout tab open, or anyone calling the action directly, places an order linked to their customer id and saved address with no valid consent. The design says validation sits at the trust boundary and here the only gate is the page. The fix added here is exactly the gate the voice channel was later found to lack.
nodes.norm_label: m1 sec-4 — placeorderaction checks only for a session, not for live consent (medium)

nodes.label: M1 SEC-5 — webhook PII stripping is incomplete (medium)
nodes.rationale: stripContact removes only two fields, but a real payment_link.paid event also carries customer contact, email and name, and a UPI vpa which is routinely the mobile number — so the phone number lands verbatim in a table outside the four allowed. Fix: strip the rest, or store only an allow-listed projection.
nodes.norm_label: m1 sec-5 — webhook pii stripping is incomplete (medium)

nodes.label: M1 SEC-6 — computable development secrets (medium)
nodes.rationale: Any reachable non-production deployment lets an attacker mint an admin platform cookie and forge OTP challenges from a value anyone can compute from the repo. The repository rule is that a missing variable is an error, never a fallback. Fix: throw unless an explicit opt-in is set, and never derive the value from a constant string.

nodes.label: M1 SEC-7 — suspension is a label with no effect (medium)
nodes.rationale: The admin-only Suspend restaurant action changes restaurant.status and nothing else: the ordering page still serves, placeOrder still takes money, and staff are still admitted.
nodes.norm_label: m1 sec-7 — suspension is a label with no effect (medium)

nodes.label: M1 SEC-8 — nag quick-pick chips store fabricated midpoints (medium)
nodes.rationale: A restaurant doing 300 aggregator orders a week records 75, and the North Star is overstated several-fold as if it were exact. Acted on differently from the suggested fix: the chips now fill the exact field so the operator sees and can correct the number before Save, keeping the range's ease without inventing a hidden point value.
nodes.norm_label: m1 sec-8 — nag quick-pick chips store fabricated midpoints (medium)

nodes.label: M1 SEC-9 — per-IP OTP limit locks out table-QR diners (medium)
nodes.rationale: Five requests per ten minutes per IP, while table-QR diners on the restaurant's Wi-Fi or behind CGNAT share one public IP, so the sixth diner in ten minutes at a busy dinner cannot order. Fix: raise the per-IP window and keep five per phone, or key the IP limit on ip plus phone hash.
nodes.norm_label: m1 sec-9 — per-ip otp limit locks out table-qr diners (medium)

nodes.label: M1 SEC-10 — lookupCustomer leaks cross-restaurant existence (low)
nodes.rationale: Any staff login can test whether a phone number has ever used any ServeLine restaurant, which crosses restaurants without consent. Fix: derive found from the restaurant-scoped profile row, and rate-limit per staff user.
nodes.norm_label: m1 sec-10 — lookupcustomer leaks cross-restaurant existence (low)

nodes.label: M1 SEC-13 — resend payment link creates a second live link (low)
nodes.rationale: Nothing cancels the first thirty-minute link, so a customer who taps both SMS messages is charged twice with no refund path. The fix went into attachPayment and closed only the resend door; the bug hunt found the same class still open through COD conversion, and found that even the resend fix only changed the bookkeeping because nothing cancels at the gateway.
nodes.norm_label: m1 sec-13 — resend payment link creates a second live link (low)

nodes.label: M1 SEC-14 — seed writes a full address into the audit log (low)
nodes.rationale: Forbidden by the repository rules and by writeAudit's own contract, and the admin audit page then displays it. Fix: audit the same redacted projection saveAddress uses.
nodes.norm_label: m1 sec-14 — seed writes a full address into the audit log (low)

nodes.label: M1 not acted on — COD auto-confirm bypasses Accept
nodes.rationale: Build Spec §5.2 decides it: cash on delivery goes to confirmed immediately if the outlet has COD enabled. The behaviour matches the spec, so the finding was closed rather than fixed.
nodes.norm_label: m1 not acted on — cod auto-confirm bypasses accept

nodes.label: M1 not acted on — address-link token mints a 30-day session
nodes.rationale: Nothing mints that token until M2's voice flow exists, and the session length is decided with that flow, not before it. A deliberate deferral rather than a dismissal.
nodes.norm_label: m1 not acted on — address-link token mints a 30-day session

nodes.label: M1 design — counter targets under 56px on the dashboard
nodes.rationale: Seen, Retry now, the sound toggle, Reopen, Add item and Sign out all shipped at the 32px dense size on the counter surface, and the sound button competed as a filled primary plate with the card primaries. The design's §6.1 minimum on the restaurant surface is 56px.
nodes.norm_label: m1 design — counter targets under 56px on the dashboard

nodes.label: M1 design — focus ring invisible on the quantity stepper
nodes.rationale: The global focus ring is a 4px outer box-shadow and the stepper's overflow:hidden clips it on all sides, while the input also sets outline:none — so keyboard focus is not visible at all, against the design's never-remove-the-ring rule.
nodes.norm_label: m1 design — focus ring invisible on the quantity stepper

nodes.label: M1 design — the Have a code? form is squashed to the right edge
nodes.rationale: The form inherits a column direction and flex-end alignment, so on a 360px phone the code input is a narrow right-hugging box with Apply underneath.
nodes.norm_label: m1 design — the have a code? form is squashed to the right edge

nodes.label: M1 design — assertive live regions used for validation errors
nodes.rationale: Five places used role=alert for validation, against the design's rule of exactly one assertive region product-wide, reserved for the new-order band.
nodes.norm_label: m1 design — assertive live regions used for validation errors

nodes.label: M1 design — favicon uses the received-state blue as decoration
nodes.rationale: A direct palette-law violation: a reserved state hue used as decoration. Fix: draw the icon in steel only.
nodes.norm_label: m1 design — favicon uses the received-state blue as decoration

nodes.label: M1 design — operator-facing copy cites an internal document
nodes.rationale: The menu empty state told the operator what the agent console does and cited Build Spec §8. Fix: say what to do and drop the citation.
nodes.norm_label: m1 design — operator-facing copy cites an internal document

nodes.label: M2 SEC-1 — the caller's spoken address is stored as a label and reaches the prompt (high)
nodes.rationale: capture_rough_address stored the spoken line as label, so the next call's system prompt carried the full address and the use_saved_address tool result returned it in the LLM request body. Build Spec §5.5 and §10 and the design allow labels only, and the tests only ever saw seeded Home labels, so the leak was untested. Fix: label null and line1 text, fall back to area, and add a rough-address row to the prompt test.
nodes.norm_label: m2 sec-1 — the caller's spoken address is stored as a label and reaches the prompt (high)

nodes.label: M2 SEC-2 — place_order writes a profile row with no consent check (high)
nodes.rationale: Unlike the web checkout, the voice place_order ran no order_fulfilment consent check, so an order was created and a customer_restaurant profile row written for a caller who had never agreed to anything. The call page's own copy claimed place_order refuses consent_required; nothing did. This finding is the origin of ADR 0005 — the gate went in and then made the assistant useless to the stranger the product exists for, which is what required a spoken-consent tool.
nodes.norm_label: m2 sec-2 — place_order writes a profile row with no consent check (high)

nodes.label: M2 SEC-3 — address read-back is bypassable (medium)
nodes.rationale: loop.ts pre-set session.addressId to the first saved address, so a delivery order succeeded without use_saved_address ever being called and the last-used label was never read back; a test demonstrated it. Only the prompt asked for the read-back. Fix: make the tools the only setters so an unconfirmed delivery returns address_required.
nodes.norm_label: m2 sec-3 — address read-back is bypassable (medium)

nodes.label: M2 SEC-4 — a parked handoff order behaves like a placed order (medium)
nodes.rationale: The caller hears connecting you to the restaurant and then gets order confirmed, pay here, for an order the counter may cancel — and their next greeting offers the abandoned cart as same as last time. Build Spec §5.2 refreshes the usual order only if the order completes. Fix: a parked flag that suppresses the payment link, both SMS and the usual-order write.
nodes.norm_label: m2 sec-4 — a parked handoff order behaves like a placed order (medium)

nodes.label: M2 SEC-5 — same as last time is not the same order (medium)
nodes.rationale: The greeting prices the usual order with variants and options but the prompt names only the item, so the model re-adds the base item and the order charges less than the quoted figure. Fix: carry variant and option names in the summary and pre-seed the session with the stored ids so add_to_cart can carry them.
nodes.norm_label: m2 sec-5 — same as last time is not the same order (medium)

nodes.label: M2 SEC-6 — vendor error text may quote request content (low-medium)
nodes.rationale: Both LLM adapters surface the provider's own error message, which embeds the response JSON, so a 400 validation message can quote request content — contrary to the comment one line above. Fix: log only the provider and status, or the error name.
nodes.norm_label: m2 sec-6 — vendor error text may quote request content (low-medium)

nodes.label: M2 SEC-7 — a spoken phone number lands on a fifth table (low)
nodes.rationale: call_turn.text is stored unsanitised, so a number the caller says is stored outside the four tables the repository rules allow. Fix: sanitise at appendTurn, or record the departure in the design.
nodes.norm_label: m2 sec-7 — a spoken phone number lands on a fifth table (low)

nodes.label: M2 SEC-8 — handoff_reason carries non-handoff values (low)
nodes.rationale: hangup, simulator_hangup, pagehide and customer_done are written into call.handoff_reason on completed and abandoned calls; the list page renders it as a handoff reason and the §12 metrics will read it.
nodes.norm_label: m2 sec-8 — handoff_reason carries non-handoff values (low)

nodes.label: M2 SEC-9 — the voice service token is global and unrated (low)
nodes.rationale: The token is not scoped to an outlet as §5.6 requires and can post turns into any live customer mic call, while a customer cookie can open unbounded sessions, each costing a call row and LLM spend, with no rate limit.
nodes.norm_label: m2 sec-9 — the voice service token is global and unrated (low)

nodes.label: M2 not acted on — the mock never takes the read-back path
nodes.rationale: The mock is a test policy; the read-back rule is enforced on the real model by the prompt and is exercised the first time a Gemini key is configured. Changing the mock would also change the acceptance conversations' turn counts for no product gain.
nodes.norm_label: m2 not acted on — the mock never takes the read-back path

nodes.label: M2 design — transcript lines carry no lang attribute
nodes.rationale: Hindi and Kannada turns sit on an English page with no language attribute, in the console review screen, its tool-call blocks and the simulator — against the design's rule that lang goes on any element whose content differs in language from the page. The simulator case needs a lang on the AI reply, which the turn result does not currently return.
nodes.norm_label: m2 design — transcript lines carry no lang attribute

nodes.label: M2 design — the customer transcript loses list semantics on WebKit
nodes.rationale: Safari and VoiceOver drop the list role when list-style is none, so the iPhone customer hears loose text instead of a list of N items with speaker names. Add role=list.
nodes.norm_label: m2 design — the customer transcript loses list semantics on webkit

nodes.label: M2 design — brand colour on a non-permitted surface
nodes.rationale: The caller's transcript bubbles used the brand wash. The design's permitted list for the customer page is short on purpose and a chat bubble is not a selected row.
nodes.norm_label: m2 design — brand colour on a non-permitted surface

nodes.label: M2 design — UI copy cites internal documents and milestones
nodes.rationale: Ideation §10, Build Spec §8 and M2b appear in console copy, and the simulator hint leaks the consent_required enum and the place_order tool name as user copy.
nodes.norm_label: m2 design — ui copy cites internal documents and milestones

nodes.label: M2 design — four polite live regions at once on the customer call page
nodes.rationale: A screen-reader user hears each AI reply from speech synthesis and again from the live region. No assertive region anywhere, which is the part that is clean.
nodes.norm_label: m2 design — four polite live regions at once on the customer call page

nodes.label: M2 design — what the review verified as clean
nodes.rationale: No raw brand hex; no 500/600 weights, letter-spacing or uppercase on translatable strings; no full-radius pills; customer surface on one elevation; all customer targets at 56px; every input with a visible label; correct per-line lang on the customer transcript; no animation beyond a transform-only press with reduced motion covered; no webfont; no assertive region.
nodes.norm_label: m2 design — what the review verified as clean

nodes.label: ServeLine App Icon
nodes.rationale: 32x32 SVG favicon. Three stacked rectangles, no type, no food imagery, no gradient: a steel-900 (#192227) rounded square ground (rx=4), an inset 20x20 steel-050 (#EDF1F3) plate (rx=2), and a 4px-wide steel-400 (#85949E) strip down the plate's left edge (rx=1). The mark is an abstraction of the order card itself: a pale enamel plate fixed to dark steel with a vertical edge band where the card carries its state edge. The band is neutral grey, not a state colour, so the product's identity mark carries no enamel meaning.

nodes.label: Today Dashboard
nodes.rationale: The owner's proof-of-value surface, titled 'Today and this month'. Shell: ServeLine wordmark, outlet name 'Kadamba Tiffin Room, Koramangala', Sign out, and a seven-tab rail (Board, New order, Menu, Cards, Today, Settings, Billing) with Today underlined. Body is a wrapping row of five white stat cards over the steel-050 app ground, then three full-width white table panels. Zero chroma on the entire surface: no charts, no coloured accents, no illustrations. Hierarchy is carried purely by type size, with 40px+ tabular numerals against small steel-500 labels.

nodes.label: Order Board
nodes.rationale: The counter's live order queue and the product's centrepiece surface. Single column of order cards on the steel-050 ground, '7 orders today' counter at top left, a 'Tap to enable order sounds' button at top right, and a collapsed 'Done, 1' group at the bottom. Cards appear in the order #5, #2, #3, #4, #6, #7: neither number order nor state order, so positions are stable for an order's whole life rather than re-sorting as state changes. Roughly 90 percent of the vertical space is given to the cards themselves; chrome is two lines.

nodes.label: Customer Ordering Page
nodes.rationale: The diner-facing self-serve ordering surface at /r/<slug>, and also the name of one of the three order channels. A full-bleed deep-green house band carries the restaurant name and a Language selector (English); everything below returns to the steel-050 ground. Order: fulfilment context 'Delivery, Koramangala', a promo notice, a labelled 'Search the menu' input, a category tab rail, then menu item rows in a white card. Narrow single column centred on a wide viewport, sized for a phone first.

nodes.label: Agent Console
nodes.rationale: The internal platform-operator surface, labelled 'ServeLine agent console' beside the wordmark. Navigation is three items: Restaurants, Mock SMS inbox, Styleguide, with the signed-in principal shown as 'agent'. The surface carries no restaurant colour and no order-state colour at all: it is pure steel, with the only filled element being the steel-900 'Add restaurant' button.

nodes.label: Restaurants List
nodes.rationale: Title 'Restaurants' with the subtitle '1 on the platform', a filter bar (Search by 'Name or slug', Stage select, Status select, Apply), and a seven-column table: Restaurant, Status, Stage, Outlets, Last order, Needs attention, Created. The single row reads 'Kadamba Tiffin Room /r/demo', Trialing, Taking orders, 1 outlet, last order 20 Sept 2026 02:23, needs attention 1, created 20 Sept 2026 02:11. Counts are right-aligned in tabular figures and rows are divided by a hairline rule, not by fill. No empty-state illustration below the single row: the layout is tuned for a table that will grow.

nodes.label: Order Card
nodes.rationale: One card is one order, bounded by a white ground and a 4px state-coloured left edge. Anatomy, top to bottom: large order number (#5), a rectangular status plate carrying a glyph plus a word, an elapsed timer right-aligned (17:40, 58:40, 39:40, 22:40, 09:40, 04:40); a fulfilment line in small caps (DELIVERY / PICKUP / TABLE 12) with area, and the channel right-aligned (Entered by staff / Ordering page / Table QR); a one-line summary '4 items, Rs400.00, Cash on delivery' with a chevron to expand; then one full-width steel-900 next-action button (Confirm order, Mark delivered, Mark collected, Mark ready, Accept order) beside a small outlined '...' overflow. The needs-attention card additionally carries a pink wash strip reading 'Call dropped before the address was complete. Call the customer back to confirm it.'

nodes.label: Dashboard Tab Navigation
nodes.rationale: Seven text tabs shared by every restaurant-side surface: Board, New order, Menu, Cards, Today, Settings, Billing. The active tab is marked by weight plus a dark underline, never by a colour fill or a pill, so the nav costs no chroma.

nodes.label: Mock SMS Inbox
nodes.rationale: A first-class navigation item in the agent console, not a debug route. Shipping a mock SMS destination as a visible console surface is the vendor-adapter build mode made operable: OTP and notification traffic can be read end to end with no SMS vendor account.

nodes.label: Styleguide
nodes.rationale: Third navigation item in the agent console: a living rendering of the design tokens and components inside the running app rather than a static document.

nodes.label: Orders today
nodes.rationale: First stat card, value 8. The same count appears on the board as the plain-language line '7 orders today'; the two captures differ by one, so they were taken at different points against the seed data.

nodes.label: Orders this month
nodes.rationale: Second stat card, value 8, equal to today's count because the seeded month has only one trading day.

nodes.label: Direct Order Share
nodes.rationale: Third stat card, shown as '4%' with the comparison line 'Last month 0%'. It is the only stat card that carries a period-over-period comparison, which marks it as the surface's proof metric: the share of the restaurant's orders that arrive direct rather than through an aggregator. It is given no more visual weight than its neighbours, so the hierarchy is stated by the comparison line rather than by size or colour.

nodes.label: AI calls used
nodes.rationale: Fourth stat card, reading '0 / 500' with the note 'The call assistant arrives with M2'. The allowance denominator is rendered even though the feature does not exist yet, and the card is not hidden or disabled: the roadmap is stated in place rather than in a separate changelog.

nodes.label: Estimated invoice to date
nodes.rationale: Fifth stat card, Rs5,015.56, explained inline as 'Subscription plus 2% on delivered direct orders'. It is placed on the operational dashboard rather than hidden behind the Billing tab, and the pricing rule is restated beneath the number so the owner can check the arithmetic.

nodes.label: Orders by channel
nodes.rationale: Four-column table: Channel, Today, This month, Value this month. Rows: Table QR 2 / 2 / Rs535.00, Ordering page 4 / 4 / Rs1,686.00, Entered by staff 2 / 2 / Rs915.00. Rendered as a plain table with no bar chart or donut: the three channels are compared by reading the figures.

nodes.label: Top customers this week
nodes.rationale: Three columns: Customer, Orders, Value. Five rows: Arjun Mehta Rs558.00, +919900000002 Rs513.00, +919900000009 Rs400.00, +919900000008 Rs340.00, Divya Hegde Rs315.00. Every customer has exactly one order, so the ranking is by value.

nodes.label: Top dishes this month
nodes.rationale: Two columns: Dish, Plates. Filter Coffee 6, Masala Dosa 5, Tandoori Roti 4, Chicken Donne Biryani 3, Butter Naan 3. The count column is labelled 'Plates', in the kitchen's own unit rather than 'Quantity'.

nodes.label: Customer name falls back to phone number
nodes.source_location: Top customers this week, rows 2 to 4
nodes.rationale: AMBIGUOUS. Three of five rows identify the customer by a full E.164 phone number rather than a name, so an unnamed customer is displayed by number. Whether this is a deliberate identity fallback or an artefact of seed data that gave only two customers names cannot be told from the screenshot alone.
nodes.norm_label: customer name falls back to phone number

nodes.label: Table QR
nodes.rationale: Order channel. Named as a row in Orders by channel and again as the right-aligned provenance label on board cards #4 and #7, both of which are TABLE orders paying at table.

nodes.label: Entered by staff
nodes.rationale: Order channel for orders keyed in at the counter, reached through the 'New order' tab. Appears as the provenance label on board cards #5 and #3. Counted as a direct channel but distinct from the self-serve ones.

nodes.label: Needs attention
nodes.rationale: The loudest state in the system: crimson 4px card edge, filled crimson plate carrying a warning triangle plus the words 'Needs attention', and a pink wash strip holding the specific reason in crimson text. It is the only state that earns a second block of copy on the card. The same concept appears as a column on the agent console's restaurants table, so it escalates from the order to the account.

nodes.label: Preparing
nodes.rationale: Mid-weight brass plate, visibly duller than the blue and green states, matching the rule that only three states are permitted to be chromatically loud. Next action is 'Mark ready'.

nodes.label: Ready
nodes.rationale: Green plate and green card edge. On the pickup order the next action is 'Mark collected'.

nodes.label: On the way
nodes.rationale: Green plate and edge, delivery-only state between ready and delivered. Next action is 'Mark delivered'.

nodes.label: New
nodes.rationale: Blue plate and edge, the arrival state. Next action is 'Accept order'. Note the naming gap: the design language calls this state 'received', the shipped chip says 'New'.

nodes.label: Done
nodes.rationale: Terminal orders are not cards at all: they collapse into a single grey line reading 'Done, 1' at the foot of the board, with no colour, no timer and no action. Finished work is drained to steel and takes one row of space.

nodes.label: Elapsed Timer
nodes.rationale: An mm:ss age counter in large tabular figures on every live card, given the same type size as the order number. It is always visible rather than revealed on expand, which makes ageing readable across the whole board at a glance.

nodes.label: Order sounds
nodes.rationale: A persistent outlined button reading 'Tap to enable order sounds'. It occupies the only chrome position on the board, acknowledging that browser autoplay policy needs a user gesture before the counter can rely on an audible new-order alert.

nodes.label: Fulfilment Type
nodes.rationale: Three values, rendered in small caps on the card's second line: DELIVERY (with the area, e.g. Koramangala), PICKUP, and TABLE followed by the table number set in a larger figure. The ordering page states the same thing in sentence case as 'Delivery, Koramangala'.

nodes.label: Cash on delivery
nodes.rationale: Payment state shown as the third element of the card summary line, alongside 'Paid' and 'Pay at table'. Payment is plain text in the summary, never a coloured badge, so it cannot compete with the state plate.

nodes.label: Pay at table
nodes.rationale: Payment state used by both Table QR orders: the diner orders from the table without paying up front and settles at the counter.

nodes.label: Menu Item Row
nodes.rationale: Row anatomy: veg mark, dish name in bold, a one-line description in steel-500 ('Crisp dosa with potato palya, sambar and two chutneys'), the price right-aligned in tabular figures (Rs70.00, Rs90.00, Rs80.00, Rs75.00, Rs95.00), and an outlined Add button beneath the price in the restaurant's colour. No dish photography and no quantity stepper until an item is added. Rows are divided by a hairline and are roughly 108px tall, sized for a thumb.

nodes.label: Veg Mark
nodes.rationale: The Indian regulatory green square with an inset green dot, drawn to the FSSAI convention rather than invented. It sits before the dish name where an Indian diner expects it, and it is the only saturated mark inside the menu card.

nodes.label: Search the menu
nodes.rationale: A full-width text input with a visible persistent label rather than a placeholder-only field or a search icon that expands, which is the correct choice for a low-tech-comfort audience. Its border is a steel control border, not a house colour.

nodes.label: Menu Category Tabs
nodes.rationale: A horizontal rail of five category jumps: South Indian Tiffin, North Indian Mains, Breads, Rice & Biryani, Beverages. Categories are text with a rule beneath, and the sections they point at are then rendered in full with their own headings, so the rail scrolls rather than filters.

nodes.label: Promo Code
nodes.rationale: A single quiet notice reading '10% off applied with code WELCOME10', set as bold steel text on a steel-100 wash with a green left bar. It states an applied fact rather than advertising an offer: no ribbon, no countdown, no second offer, and no colour beyond the 4px house bar.

nodes.label: Language Selector
nodes.rationale: A labelled select reading 'Language: English' in the header band, given equal prominence to the restaurant name. Placing it in the topmost band rather than in a footer treats multilingual diners as the default case, not an accessibility afterthought.

nodes.label: Cart
nodes.rationale: AMBIGUOUS. No cart, running total or checkout affordance is visible anywhere in this capture, and the screenshot is cropped mid-row on 'Bisi Bele Bath' with its Add button clipped. Whether the cart is a sticky bottom bar that appears after the first Add, a separate step, or simply below the fold cannot be determined from this image.

nodes.label: Trialing
nodes.rationale: Account status, rendered as an outlined rectangular plate in steel rather than a filled colour chip: an account status is not an order state, so it is denied enamel.

nodes.label: Taking orders
nodes.rationale: Onboarding stage, held in a column separate from Status and set as plain text with no chip at all. Splitting commercial status from onboarding stage lets the console answer 'are they live?' and 'are they paying?' independently.

nodes.label: Voice Call Assistant
nodes.rationale: Named on the shipped M1 surface twice before it exists: the AI calls card says 'The call assistant arrives with M2', and board card #5 carries the failure copy 'Call dropped before the address was complete', which is the human fallback the assistant will hand off to.

nodes.label: Vendor Mock Mode
nodes.rationale: Every external vendor sits behind an adapter interface with a working mock, so the product runs end to end with no vendor account. The agent console's Mock SMS inbox is this policy surfaced as a usable screen.

nodes.label: Money in paise
nodes.rationale: Money is stored as integer paise and never as floats. Every money figure on the shipped surfaces renders with exactly two decimal places, including the fee-derived Rs5,015.56 and the menu's Rs70.00.

nodes.label: Steel & Enamel
nodes.rationale: The design language: a working steel counter with flat enamel plates fixed to it. Steel is ServeLine's and never carries meaning; enamel belongs to the order or to the restaurant.

nodes.label: Two layers, they never mix
nodes.rationale: State enamel and house enamel never occupy the same component, which is how a restaurant's brand colour can equal a state colour without collision.

nodes.label: Fixed positions, the board never re-sorts
nodes.rationale: An order's position is stable for its whole life so the operator's eye learns where things are; arrivals are announced by a counter at the top, never by pushing the board around under a moving finger.
nodes.norm_label: fixed positions, the board never re-sorts

nodes.label: Isolated destruction
nodes.rationale: 'Cancel order' is never adjacent to 'Mark ready'; destructive actions are deliberately separated from the dominant next action.

nodes.label: House Enamel
nodes.rationale: The restaurant's own colour. Permitted only on the customer header band, the customer primary CTA, the active tab and the logo chip; never on the dashboard board, the agent console, or any state channel.

nodes.label: State Enamel
nodes.rationale: The order lifecycle's colour. Permitted only on the card edge, the status plate and the state glyph; never as decoration or as a page field.

nodes.label: Tabular figures
nodes.rationale: Kept from the rejected kitchen-ticket direction: tabular figures for every number, so columns of money and counts align without adopting a monospace face that cannot cover three scripts.

nodes.label: Anti-aggregator
nodes.rationale: The category rut the system refuses: orange chrome, food photography carousels and promo ribbons, enforced as a numeric distance rather than a preference.

nodes.label: --steel-900 (#192227)
nodes.rationale: Primary text and primary button fill, 16.16:1 on white.

nodes.label: --steel-050 (#EDF1F3)
nodes.rationale: The app ground: the pale blue-green grey behind every card on all four shipped surfaces.

nodes.label: --steel-400 (#85949E)
nodes.rationale: Minimum control and input border at 3.12:1, and disabled text.

nodes.label: Call Review Page
nodes.rationale: Agent-console surface at Calls / <call id>. Two-column layout: a full turn-by-turn Transcript on the left with inline tool-call args/results, and a right rail of four cards (Call, Tag, Cost, Order). This is the after-the-fact audit surface for a single call.

nodes.label: Call Simulator
nodes.rationale: Agent-console page titled 'Call simulator'. Subtitle reads: 'A real call row with transport = browser, driven by text. What the model does with each message shows under its reply.' Shows a live Conversation panel with call id, End call button, a 'Caller says' input and a Language select (Hindi). Vendor-free way to exercise the assistant.

nodes.label: Customer Call Page
nodes.rationale: Customer-facing browser-call surface, outlet-branded header 'Kadamba Tiffin Room' with a Language selector (English). Chat bubbles alternate restaurant/You, with a primary 'Tap to speak' button, a 'Type instead' input + Send, and 'End call'. Footer: 'Ordering by ServeLine'.

nodes.label: Spoken Consent
nodes.rationale: Consent is obtained by the assistant speaking a notice and the caller answering aloud ('haan theek hai'), then recorded via record_consent {"agreed":true} before the order can be placed.

nodes.label: Consent Notice
nodes.rationale: Spoken verbatim in Hindi before ordering: the outlet will keep the caller's number, name and address to deliver the order, plus what they ordered before so next time is quicker; only Kadamba Tiffin Room sees it; it does not go to any other restaurant; the caller can ask for it to be removed at any time; the full notice is on the outlet's ordering page; ends with 'ठीक है?' (is that alright?).

nodes.label: consent_required
nodes.rationale: Refusal reason returned by place_order when consent has not yet been recorded: result {"ok": false, "reason": "consent_required"}, shown in the trace as 'place_order ... -> refused: consent_required - 2 ms'.

nodes.label: record_consent
nodes.rationale: Voice tool called with args {"agreed": true}, returning {"ok": true, "data": {"agreed": true}} in 11 ms, immediately after the caller says 'haan theek hai' and immediately before the successful place_order.

nodes.label: place_order
nodes.rationale: Voice tool called with args {"fulfilment":"pickup","payment_method":"upi_link"}. First call refused with consent_required (2 ms); after record_consent the same call succeeds (28 ms) returning orderId, statusUrl, totalPaise 18000, totalRupees '180', paymentMethod 'upi_link', paymentLinkSent true.

nodes.label: search_menu
nodes.rationale: Voice tool called with {"query":"masala dosa","language":"hi"}; returns the matching menu items with ids, variants, pricePaise/priceRupees and optionGroups (e.g. Extras with Extra chutney, Extra ghee, maxSelect 2). Latency shown (5-7 ms).

nodes.label: add_to_cart
nodes.rationale: Voice tool called with {"item_id": ..., "qty": n} and optionally "variant_id"; returns the whole cart with lines, lineId, linePaise, totalPaise, discountPaise and subtotalPaise.

nodes.label: get_cart
nodes.rationale: Voice tool called with {} before the order read-back; returns the current cart so the assistant can recite the order and total before asking pickup or delivery.

nodes.label: Tool Call Trace
nodes.rationale: Every tool invocation is rendered under the assistant turn that made it. The simulator shows a one-line form (name, args JSON, arrow, ok/refused, latency in ms); the call review page shows the full two-column args / result JSON. This is how the product proves what the assistant actually did, not just what it said.

nodes.label: Transcript
nodes.rationale: Left column of the call review page, headed '11 turns - confidence from the recogniser, low below 0.6' (9 turns on the consent call). Columns: #, Who (AI / Caller), Said, Lang, Conf., At (elapsed timestamp plus a per-turn duration).

nodes.label: Recogniser Confidence
nodes.rationale: Per-turn 'Conf.' column with the header rule 'confidence from the recogniser, low below 0.6'. Values render as '-' on these browser-transport calls because no speech recogniser ran.

nodes.label: Call Cost Ledger
nodes.rationale: 'Cost' card on the call review page, itemised per vendor concern: LLM (with token counts, e.g. 12079 in / 114 out; 10678 in / 110 out on the consent call), SMS, Telephony, STT (with seconds), TTS (with characters), then a bold Total. All rupee figures are 0.00 because the call ran on mocks.

nodes.label: LLM Token Usage
nodes.rationale: Input/output token counts recorded alongside the LLM line of the cost ledger ('12079 in / 114 out'), so the cost can be recomputed when a real model price is attached.

nodes.label: Call Record
nodes.rationale: 'Call' card fields: Outlet, Transport, Caller (pseudonymous 'customer 03015ff1' / 'customer 57ec8653' rather than a phone number), Started, Ended, Duration (143 s), Language (hi), Intent (Order / Unknown), Outcome (Completed / live), Handoff reason (simulator_hangup), Answered by (Ai), Counts toward allowance.

nodes.label: Browser Transport
nodes.rationale: Transport = 'Browser' on both reviewed calls, and the simulator subtitle says it creates 'a real call row with transport = browser'. Evidence that a call is a first-class record independent of any telephony vendor.

nodes.label: Call Allowance
nodes.rationale: 'Counts toward allowance' field. On the completed call: 'Yes - flagged, but browser calls are not billed'. On the live consent call: 'No'. The allowance decision is computed and explained on the record itself.

nodes.label: Failure Tag
nodes.rationale: 'Tag' card with a Failure select (default 'Not tagged') and a Save button. Header note on the completed call: "For M4's tuning loop (Build Spec §8)"; on the consent call: 'Tag what went wrong; tags feed the menu-vocabulary tuning'.

nodes.label: Menu Vocabulary Tuning
nodes.rationale: Named destination for failure tags: 'tags feed the menu-vocabulary tuning'. Ties the review surface to a later tuning loop rather than to a dead-end support queue.

nodes.label: Order
nodes.rationale: 'Order' card: Order 6abe5feb, Status badge 'Awaiting payment', Channel 'Phone call', Fulfilment 'Pickup', Items '1x Paneer Butter Masala - Full, 1x Masala Dosa, 1x Filter Coffee - Large', Total ₹375.00, Payment 'UPI link - Awaiting payment', Placed 21 Sept 2026, 10:02. On the consent call the same card reads 'No order from this call.'

nodes.label: UPI Link
nodes.rationale: payment_method 'upi_link' in the place_order args, paymentLinkSent: true in its result, 'Payment: UPI link - Awaiting payment' on the Order card, and the assistant's closing line 'पेमेंट लिंक SMS से आ रहा है' (the payment link is coming by SMS).

nodes.label: Order Status URL
nodes.rationale: place_order returns a statusUrl of the form http://localhost:3000/r/demo/order/<orderId> alongside the orderId, giving the caller a web surface to track an order placed by voice.

nodes.label: Repeat Order Suggestion
nodes.rationale: Opening line to a known caller: 'Hello Divya, welcome back to Kadamba Tiffin Room. Same as last time - 1 Paneer Butter Masala, 1 Masala Dosa, 1 Filter Coffee, ₹375?' The order-history retention promised in the consent notice is what makes this possible.

nodes.label: Tap to Speak
nodes.rationale: Primary full-width button on the customer call page, in the outlet's teal brand colour.

nodes.label: Type Instead Fallback
nodes.rationale: Labelled 'Type instead': a text input plus Send sitting directly under 'Tap to speak', so a caller in a noisy place or with a failing recogniser can continue the same call by typing.

nodes.label: Language Selection
nodes.rationale: A Language select on both the simulator ('Hindi') and the customer call page ('English'), a per-turn Lang column in the transcript, and a 'language' argument passed into search_menu.

nodes.label: Hindi
nodes.rationale: The assistant replies in Devanagari Hindi to romanised-Hindi caller input ('do masala dosa' -> 'जोड़ दिया| अभी तक: 2 × Masala Dosa — ₹180.00| और कुछ?'), keeping English dish names inline. Lang column value 'hi'.

nodes.label: Kadamba Tiffin Room
nodes.rationale: Seeded demo outlet, shown as 'Kadamba Tiffin Room · Koramangala' on the call review page and as the branded header and speaker name on the customer call page.

nodes.label: DPDP Act
nodes.rationale: INFERRED: the statute is never named on screen, but the spoken notice has the DPDP shape - stated purpose, named data categories, no onward sharing, a withdrawal/erasure right, a pointer to the full notice, and an explicit yes recorded before processing.

nodes.label: Consent Gate
nodes.rationale: INFERRED: place_order is refused rather than the model merely being told to ask first. The tool layer itself rejects with consent_required until record_consent has run, so the guardrail survives a model that skips the script.

nodes.label: Pseudonymous Caller ID
nodes.rationale: The Caller field on the review page shows 'customer 03015ff1' / 'customer 57ec8653' - an opaque id, never a phone number, on a surface a support agent reads.

nodes.label: Handoff Reason
nodes.rationale: Field on the Call card; value 'simulator_hangup' on the completed call, '-' on the live one. Records why the assistant stopped handling the call.

nodes.label: Tool Latency
nodes.rationale: Every tool call is stamped with a duration (search_menu 5-7 ms, add_to_cart 0-1 ms, get_cart 0 ms, record_consent 11 ms, place_order 2 ms refused / 28 ms ok), making the assistant's turn budget inspectable.

nodes.label: ADR 0008 — ShadCN supplies the primitives; Steel & Enamel keeps the look
nodes.rationale: Accepted 23 September 2026. Amends app/globals.css's "never a utility class" rule and makes ADR 0002 §3's dark mode load-bearing for a second consumer. The ask was "a clean UI in light and dark, built with ShadCN"; the ADR splits that into mechanics (adopted) and appearance (refused).
nodes.norm_label: adr 0008 — shadcn supplies the primitives; steel & enamel keeps the look

nodes.label: ADR 0009 — Speech to text is an adapter, and it runs on the restaurant's own machine
nodes.rationale: Accepted 23 September 2026. Follows ADR 0007 (which measured whisper and left it unwired) and ADR 0004 (the brain in TypeScript). Amends Build Spec §3 (Sarvam as the speech vendor) and §5.6 (the voice service contract).
nodes.norm_label: adr 0009 — speech to text is an adapter, and it runs on the restaurant's own machine

nodes.label: ShadCN for the primitives the repository lacks, not for its appearance
nodes.rationale: Two facts made this a design decision rather than an install. There is already a researched design language (Steel & Enamel, WCAG ratios computed in the palette comments, named laws: colour is never a button, plates not pills, never colour alone, delivered returns to steel, seams not shadows) and ShadCN ships its own look — neutral greys, rounded pills, soft shadows, colour as the primary action. Adopting that look wholesale would discard the research and make the product resemble every other dashboard in the category. Against that, the thirteen existing src/ui components cover cards, chips, fields and steppers well but there is no Select, Dialog, Tabs, Popover, Tooltip, DropdownMenu or Switch — exactly the components where hand-rolling reliably produces accessibility defects: focus trapping, roving tabindex, aria-expanded, Escape handling, returning focus to the trigger on close. So: mechanics adopted, appearance refused, the thirteen existing components untouched.
nodes.norm_label: shadcn for the primitives the repository lacks, not for its appearance

nodes.label: shadcn-bridge.css — every semantic utility resolves to a Steel & Enamel token
nodes.rationale: Tailwind v4's `@theme inline` gives each semantic utility a var(--token) as its value, verified in the compiled stylesheet. `inline` is what makes it work: without it Tailwind copies today's computed value into its own variable, which would snapshot the light palette and break dark mode. The bridge is one file and it is the seam between the two styling idioms.
nodes.norm_label: shadcn-bridge.css — every semantic utility resolves to a steel & enamel token

nodes.label: A utility that does not resolve to a token is a bug, not a shortcut
nodes.rationale: globals.css's rule was amended rather than deleted. Its letter was "no utility classes in src/ui"; its purpose was "a component cannot introduce a colour, a radius or a font the design system has not decided". The purpose is preserved exactly because there is not one raw value in the bridge, only var(--token).
nodes.norm_label: a utility that does not resolve to a token is a bug, not a shortcut

nodes.label: No .dark class, no next-themes, no dark: utility
nodes.rationale: tokens.css already re-points every role under [data-theme="dark"] and under prefers-color-scheme, so a primitive that reads the bridge is correct in both themes with no dark: utility. A dark: utility inside a primitive is a second source of truth and gets deleted rather than fixed. The @custom-variant dark in the bridge exists only so that any that survive agree with the tokens around them.
nodes.norm_label: no .dark class, no next-themes, no dark: utility

nodes.label: One Button, not two
nodes.rationale: `shadcn add` pulled its own button.tsx, which would have put two different buttons in a codebase whose brief was consistency. It was deleted and Dialog and AlertDialog were rewired to src/ui/Button.tsx, whose `danger` variant already carries the design's §11.1 note that it is permitted only inside a destructive confirm. `asChild` moved onto the Radix primitive, since our Button renders a real <button> or <a> and has no Slot.
