nodes.label: Six new dependencies, measured against the ordering page's Lighthouse budget
nodes.rationale: radix-ui, lucide-react, class-variance-authority, clsx, tailwind-merge and sonner are new. CLAUDE.md forbids adding a dependency for what a few lines of standard library would do — but focus trapping and roving tabindex are not that. ADR 0003 holds the customer ordering page to Lighthouse mobile ≥ 85 and it currently measures 99, so every primitive introduced on the customer ordering path must be measured against that budget before it ships, and a primitive that costs more than it earns there belongs on the staff surfaces only.
nodes.norm_label: six new dependencies, measured against the ordering page's lighthouse budget

nodes.label: A second styling idiom now exists in src/ui
nodes.rationale: Accepted cost: a reader must know that primitives/* is utility-classed and everything else is CSS modules. Mitigated by the seam being a single file.
nodes.norm_label: a second styling idiom now exists in src/ui

nodes.label: Each primitive is a file in the repository, not a package import
nodes.rationale: Replacing a primitive means editing it. Removing ShadCN entirely means deleting src/ui/primitives/, the bridge and six dependencies; nothing outside those files knows ShadCN exists.
nodes.norm_label: each primitive is a file in the repository, not a package import

nodes.label: Speech to text becomes an adapter in src/adapters/stt/
nodes.rationale: Same shape as src/adapters/llm/: an interface, a mock that needs nothing, and providers selected by STT_PROVIDER. Keeps the build-mode promise that a real vendor account is a new implementation of the same interface plus an environment variable, never a change to calling code.
nodes.norm_label: speech to text becomes an adapter in src/adapters/stt/

nodes.label: Bytes in, text out — a deliberately transport-shaped interface
nodes.rationale: {audio, mimeType, lang} to {text, confidence, seconds, provider, model}. Shaped this way so the browser can post a clip it recorded and the Python/Exotel transport can post a clip it cut from the line, and neither knows which recogniser answered.
nodes.norm_label: bytes in, text out — a deliberately transport-shaped interface

nodes.label: Whisper on the restaurant's own machine
nodes.rationale: whisper is the default real provider and it runs locally: a whisper.cpp server on the restaurant's own machine, addressed by WHISPER_HOST. No account, no per-minute price, and the audio never leaves the building — a stronger answer to Build Spec §10's data-residency question than Sarvam can give, because Sarvam is still a network hop out of the restaurant. ADR 0007's 22 s cold-start figure is why this expects a server that stays up rather than a process per clip.
nodes.norm_label: whisper on the restaurant's own machine

nodes.label: sarvam is written and has never run
nodes.rationale: Build Spec §3 names it and there is no account to buy it with. It exists so that turning it on is an environment variable rather than a change to calling code, and its file says plainly that its request shape is unverified. The case for it is Kannada and telephone-band audio, where a model trained on Indian speech should beat a general one — but that is an expectation, not a measurement, and the eval set is how it gets settled the day an account appears.
nodes.norm_label: sarvam is written and has never run

nodes.label: POST /api/v1/voice/calls/{id}/listen — a separate route from /turn
nodes.rationale: Transcribing and answering are separate failures with separate costs: a clip that could not be heard should be re-recorded, not answered, and only the transport knows whether re-recording is possible. Multipart rather than JSON because base64 would inflate every clip by a third for nothing. Answers 502 when the whisper server is not there, and says where it looked.

nodes.label: The mock takes the words from the transport
nodes.rationale: A mock recogniser has an awkward problem — bytes in, words out, and no way to know which words — and a fixed sentence would make every mocked call order the same dish. So under VENDOR_MODE=mock the browser hands over the words its own recogniser heard, in a field real providers ignore, while everything else on the path runs for real: the route, the cost ledger, the confidence gate, the turn. The route refuses that field outright when a live recogniser is selected, so it can never become a way to put words in a caller's mouth.
nodes.norm_label: the mock takes the words from the transport

nodes.label: Confidence is derived, and says so
nodes.rationale: whisper.cpp reports a mean log probability per token, not a confidence. exp(avg_logprob), weighted by segment duration and reduced by no_speech_prob, is the closest honest reading — a proxy for how sure the model was of the words it chose, not a calibrated probability that the transcript is right. Build Spec §5.3 gates on 0.6 and this is the number that gate sees. Where a provider reports nothing the answer is null meaning unknown, and the gate must not read unknown as low: a recogniser that cannot report a number should not make every turn suspect.
nodes.norm_label: confidence is derived, and says so

nodes.label: The browser's SpeechRecognition is a feature of Chrome, not of this product
nodes.rationale: Three reasons it cannot be the product's recogniser: it does not exist on every browser and there is no version of it on a telephone; it sends the audio to Google whatever Build Spec §10 says about this product's data living in Mumbai, and the consent notice a caller agrees to does not mention it; and it requires a caller holding a device, which is the opposite of the premise that a customer rings a restaurant's existing number. ADR 0007's sentence that replacing it "is transport work" was load-bearing in a way it did not look — it left the phone half of a voice product never run end to end.
nodes.norm_label: the browser's speechrecognition is a feature of chrome, not of this product

nodes.label: stt_paise and stt_seconds now fill on every clip
nodes.rationale: addCost has had those ledger columns since M2 and could not accept a value for them; with an STT provider on the path they fill. Under STT_PROVIDER=whisper with a local server the charge is zero, which is the point.
nodes.norm_label: stt_paise and stt_seconds now fill on every clip

nodes.label: A clip adds ~1.9 s warm to a turn already missing the latency budget
nodes.rationale: ADR 0007 already measured 2.9 s p50 against Build Spec §5.4's 1.8 s p95 budget. Speech does not make that gap worse in kind but it makes it worse in size. The honest reading is that §5.4's budget was written for a streaming pipeline and this is not one yet.
nodes.norm_label: a clip adds ~1.9 s warm to a turn already missing the latency budget

nodes.label: Text to speech is unchanged and still open
nodes.rationale: ADR 0007 found Indic TTS locally to be the weak link — Piper's Hindi voices below Bulbul's and Kannada barely existing — and the browser's own voices still speak the reply. A telephone caller cannot hear those either, so the Exotel transport needs a TTS adapter of the same shape before a real call works end to end. This ADR does not build one.
nodes.norm_label: text to speech is unchanged and still open

nodes.label: The §16 spoken evaluation now has somewhere to send the audio
nodes.rationale: "These utterances spoken by five people down a real phone line with kitchen noise playing" is the measurement that decides a pilot, and it will be lower than the text score.
nodes.norm_label: the §16 spoken evaluation now has somewhere to send the audio

nodes.label: The Kannada 86% was a wasted tool round, not a recognition failure
nodes.source_location: ### What was wrong, and what fixed it
nodes.rationale: search_menu matches the menu as the restaurant wrote it, which is Latin script, and menu_vocabulary — the thing that would let a Kannada query match — is M4. The assistant had been compensating on its own: search ಮಸಾಲ ದೋಸೆ, get nothing, translate, search masala dosa, then add. That works, and a trace of kn-order-long shows it recovering perfectly — five empty searches, five successful ones, five correct adds. But the recovery costs a full tool round out of the four a turn allows, and nothing in the prompt told the assistant which script the menu was in, so it only translated first about half the time. The same case passed on one run and failed on the next. That variance was the entire 86%.
nodes.norm_label: the kannada 86% was a wasted tool round, not a recognition failure

nodes.label: Two prompt lines: the menu is Latin script, and a multi-dish order is searched and added all at once
nodes.source_location: ### What was wrong, and what fixed it
nodes.rationale: Telling the assistant the menu is Latin script whatever the caller speaks removes the half-the-time translate-first variance; batching a multi-dish order into one search and one add buys back the tool round the recovery costs. Both are workarounds for the M2 matcher and should be deleted when menu_vocabulary lands.
nodes.norm_label: two prompt lines: the menu is latin script, and a multi-dish order is searched and added all at once

nodes.label: npm run trace — every tool call one utterance produces, in order
nodes.rationale: When a case fails, the score alone cannot say whether the assistant misheard the caller or simply ran out of tool rounds. Printing each call with its arguments and what came back distinguishes the two immediately, and is how the Kannada finding was diagnosed.
nodes.norm_label: npm run trace — every tool call one utterance produces, in order

nodes.label: Read errored before you read the score
nodes.rationale: Errored cases (a rate limit, an outage) are excluded from both accuracies, so rate limiting does not lower a result — it raises it, by quietly removing whichever cases happened to fail while the quota was gone. A run with a double-digit errored column is an upper bound on an upper bound.
nodes.norm_label: read errored before you read the score

nodes.label: A score here is an upper bound — this is text, not speech
nodes.rationale: No recogniser, no phone line, no kitchen noise. This set holds the model, the prompt and the tools to account and will be the script the recordings read from, but a recogniser that mishears "dosa" as "dosha" fails a case this set would pass. 100% does not mean the assistant hears Kannada; it means it reasons correctly about Kannada text.
nodes.norm_label: a score here is an upper bound — this is text, not speech

nodes.label: Latency still misses Build Spec §5.4 by four to five times
nodes.rationale: §5.4 budgets p50 1.0 s and p95 1.8 s a turn; every language measures four to five times that. The accuracy problem is closed; the latency one is not.
nodes.norm_label: latency still misses build spec §5.4 by four to five times

nodes.label: A --cases run is not comparable with a full run
nodes.rationale: A score from a named-cases run covers that subset only. A misspelled id is reported rather than silently dropped, because a run that quietly scores fewer cases scores higher.
nodes.norm_label: a --cases run is not comparable with a full run

nodes.label: kerala-parotta — pieces or plates is a product decision, not a test one
nodes.rationale: The menu calls the item "Kerala Parotta (2 pcs)", so "two parotta" means pieces to a caller and orders to the menu; a trace showed the assistant adding one plate, a defensible reading. kn-order-kurma-parotta had already been reworded to "two plates"; hi-order-full-chicken-curry had not, so the set was asking the harder question in Hindi and the easier one in Kannada and the two scores were not comparable on that item. Rewording a case so it passes deserves the scrutiny it sounds like it deserves; the justification is that the utterance is genuinely ambiguous to a human too, and leaving one language on the ambiguous phrasing measured the ambiguity rather than the assistant. The ambiguity itself is still open: either the assistant asks which the caller meant, or menu items stop carrying quantities in their names.
nodes.norm_label: kerala-parotta — pieces or plates is a product decision, not a test one

nodes.label: menu_vocabulary is M4 — no Indic-script menu matching until then
nodes.source_location: ### What was wrong, and what fixed it
nodes.rationale: Known and documented limitation at src/voice/tools.ts: spoken aliases per outlet in all three languages arrive at M4, and until then a Kannada or Hindi query only matches the Latin-script menu after the assistant translates it.
nodes.norm_label: menu_vocabulary is m4 — no indic-script menu matching until then

nodes.label: src/ui/primitives — the one place utility classes are allowed
nodes.rationale: The carve-out is only safe because shadcn-bridge.css gives every utility these components use a Steel & Enamel token as its value (ADR 0008). A utility that does not resolve to a token is a bug. There is one Button and it is src/ui/Button.tsx; do not add a second. Do not add a dark: utility — tokens.css already flips. Anything added here that renders on the customer ordering page must be measured against ADR 0003's Lighthouse budget before it ships.
nodes.norm_label: src/ui/primitives — the one place utility classes are allowed

nodes.label: Do not add a dependency for something a few lines of standard library would do
nodes.rationale: A standing prohibition that ADR 0008 has to argue against explicitly: focus trapping and roving tabindex are not a few lines of standard library, which is what buys the six ShadCN dependencies their place.
nodes.norm_label: do not add a dependency for something a few lines of standard library would do

nodes.label: Current milestone M2 — the voice assistant's brain and two vendor-free transports
nodes.rationale: M1 is complete and browser-verified. A milestone is done when Build Spec §14's acceptance criteria pass, not when the code exists; where a criterion says "on a real phone", it means on a real phone.
nodes.norm_label: current milestone m2 — the voice assistant's brain and two vendor-free transports

nodes.label: STT_PROVIDER
nodes.rationale: Selects the speech-to-text provider. Per CLAUDE.md a missing vendor variable is an error, not a silent fallback to a mock; mocks are selected explicitly by VENDOR_MODE=mock.

nodes.label: WHISPER_HOST
nodes.rationale: Addresses the whisper.cpp server on the restaurant's own machine. listen answers 502 when it is not there and says where it looked.

nodes.label: answer_enquiry tool handler (src/voice/tools.ts)
nodes.rationale: Named by the eval set as one of the four expect.tool outcomes that are not a cart.

nodes.label: transfer_to_human tool handler (src/voice/tools.ts)
nodes.rationale: Named by the eval set as one of the four expect.tool outcomes that are not a cart.

nodes.label: check_serviceability tool handler (src/voice/tools.ts)
nodes.rationale: Named by the eval set as one of the four expect.tool outcomes that are not a cart.

nodes.label: apply_code tool handler (src/voice/tools.ts)
nodes.rationale: Named by the eval set as one of the four expect.tool outcomes that are not a cart.

nodes.label: src/ui/primitives — the ShadCN primitives
nodes.rationale: Select, Dialog, Tabs, Popover, Tooltip, DropdownMenu, Switch, Label and Sonner — the components where hand-rolling reliably produces accessibility defects.

nodes.label: shadcn-bridge.css
nodes.rationale: The one file that is the seam between the utility-classed primitives and the CSS-module components.

nodes.label: tokens.css
nodes.rationale: Imported unlayered so it always beats Tailwind preflight; re-points every role under [data-theme="dark"] and under prefers-color-scheme.

nodes.label: SttRequest.mockTranscript
nodes.rationale: A mock recogniser has bytes in and words out and no way to know which words. So under VENDOR_MODE=mock the transport — which does have the words, from the browser's own recogniser — says what was said. Every other part of the path runs for real: the route, the ledger, the confidence gate, the turn. Real providers never read the field, so setting it against a live recogniser changes nothing; it is not a way to put words in a caller's mouth.

nodes.label: whisper no-server error message
nodes.rationale: The usual cause of a failed fetch is that nobody started whisper-server, so the error names the host, WHISPER_HOST and docs/adr/0007 — because 'fetch failed' sends the next person looking at the network rather than at their own machine.

nodes.label: temperature 0.0 decoding
nodes.rationale: Greedy. A caller's order is not a creative writing task, and sampling costs the determinism the eval depends on.

nodes.label: BYTES_PER_SECOND heuristic
nodes.rationale: 16 kB/s, roughly Opus at what a browser MediaRecorder produces by default. A derived-but-plausible duration keeps the ledger path honest without a real decoder.

nodes.label: Sarvam reports neither confidence nor duration
nodes.rationale: Sarvam's documented response carries no per-utterance confidence, so confidence is null — 'unknown', and Build Spec §5.3's gate must not read unknown as low. Nor a duration: seconds is left at zero rather than guessed, because an invented number in call_cost is worse than a missing one when Build Spec §12's spend alert is computed from it.
nodes.norm_label: sarvam reports neither confidence nor duration

nodes.label: Sarvam error bodies are never echoed
nodes.rationale: A vendor error can quote the request, and the request is the caller's voice (CLAUDE.md, no PII in logs). A 401 becomes 'rejected the key' and everything else 'error response'.
nodes.norm_label: sarvam error bodies are never echoed

nodes.label: POST /voice/calls/{id}/listen
nodes.rationale: The missing half of the call path. /turn has always taken text, which meant the caller's voice had to be turned into words on the browser page by Chrome's own recogniser (ADR 0007) — one browser, a device the caller is holding, and audio sent to Google whatever Build Spec §10 says. A telephone caller has no browser at all, so the phone half of a voice product had never run. This is the seam the transports meet at, and neither knows which recogniser answers. Deliberately not fused with /turn: transcribing and answering are separate failures with separate costs, a clip that could not be heard should be re-recorded rather than answered, and only the transport knows whether re-recording is possible (Build Spec §5.6). Multipart rather than JSON because base64 in a JSON string would inflate every clip by a third for nothing.

nodes.label: mockTranscript refused against a live provider
nodes.rationale: A scripted transcript is accepted only when the selected adapter is itself the mock; posted against a live recogniser it is a 400, not an ignored field. Refused outright so this can never become a way to put words in a caller's mouth while the ledger, the confidence gate and the turn all run for real. mockConfidence is only honoured when finite and within 0–1.
nodes.norm_label: mocktranscript refused against a live provider

nodes.label: the clip is billed even when nothing was said
nodes.rationale: The recogniser ran and the seconds were spent. A ledger that counts only successful clips under-reports what a call actually cost, and Build Spec §12's spend alert is computed from that number. The addCost write is deliberately best-effort so a ledger failure cannot lose the transcript.
nodes.norm_label: the clip is billed even when nothing was said

nodes.label: an empty transcript is a 200, not an error
nodes.rationale: Silence is a thing a caller does. The transport decides whether to prompt again or wait, and the turn guardrails already handle an empty utterance — so the route does not invent an error for it.
nodes.norm_label: an empty transcript is a 200, not an error

nodes.label: media type normalisation and clip ceiling
nodes.rationale: A Blob's type can be empty or carry codec parameters (audio/webm;codecs=opus), so the media type alone is compared and an empty one falls back to webm, which is what a browser records by default. The accepted list is what a browser MediaRecorder and a telephony leg actually produce. 8 MB is the ceiling because past that the transport is sending a recording, not a turn.
nodes.norm_label: media type normalisation and clip ceiling

nodes.label: theme choice scoped by cookie path
nodes.rationale: ADR 0002 §3: staff surfaces get a toggle because a counter tablet's lighting has nothing to do with the tablet's OS setting — a kitchen is bright at noon and dim at 11pm and the device never hears about it. The customer ordering page deliberately has none, because a customer is trying to order food, not configure a theme. That rule is enforced by cookie path (/app, /agent) rather than by a check, so the browser sends each cookie only where it belongs and never on /r/{slug}. Widening either to path / would put a staff choice on a customer's phone.
nodes.norm_label: theme choice scoped by cookie path

nodes.label: @theme inline colour bridge
nodes.rationale: ShadCN components are written against Tailwind's semantic colour utilities — bg-background, text-muted-foreground, border-input, ring-ring. This file is the only place those names are given meaning, and every one resolves to a Steel & Enamel token. 'inline' is load-bearing: it makes Tailwind emit var(--bg-app) at the use site rather than copying today's computed value into its own variable — without it the bridge would snapshot the light palette and dark mode would stop working.

nodes.label: primitives inherit dark mode with no dark: utility
nodes.rationale: A dependency with no import: tokens.css already re-points every role under [data-theme="dark"] and under the OS media query, so a ShadCN primitive that reads --color-background follows the theme without a single dark: utility. A dark: rule inside a primitive is a second source of truth and should be deleted rather than fixed (ADR 0008).
nodes.norm_label: primitives inherit dark mode with no dark: utility

nodes.label: a primitive cannot introduce a colour
nodes.rationale: There is no raw value anywhere in the bridge — only var(--token). A utility that does not resolve to a token is a bug, not a shortcut. This is what makes src/ui/primitives/ the one place utility classes are allowed.
nodes.norm_label: a primitive cannot introduce a colour

nodes.label: radius and elevation scales re-pointed
nodes.rationale: Tailwind's own radius and shadow scales are overwritten so rounded-md and shadow-md cannot mean Tailwind's idea of them. --radius-xs is bridged although nothing uses it: left alone it stays Tailwind's raw 0.125rem, so the first primitive to reach for rounded-xs would silently ship a value the design system never decided — the ADR 0008 failure mode, cheaper to close than to detect. Shadows map to the elevation tokens, which are a 1px ring in dark and a shadow only in light, because soft drop shadows are forbidden in dark. --radius-full stays Tailwind's and is reserved for avatars and count badges.

nodes.label: @custom-variant dark
nodes.rationale: Stock ShadCN keys dark: on a .dark class; ADR 0002 §3 keys this product on [data-theme] plus the OS setting, with an explicit light choice winning over a dark OS. Teaching Tailwind the same rule means a dark: utility that does survive into a primitive agrees with the tokens around it instead of contradicting them. Preferably it is deleted instead.

nodes.label: --font-mono, --ease-out and --ease-in deliberately omitted
nodes.rationale: tokens.css already defines those exact names at :root and is imported unlayered, so it beats Tailwind's @layer theme defaults and those utilities already resolve to Steel & Enamel values. Restating them here would be --ease-out: var(--ease-out), which is circular and silently drops the declaration. Only --ease-inout needs a line, because Tailwind spells the same curve --ease-in-out.

nodes.label: the dark palette written twice
nodes.rationale: ADR 0002 §3 gives dark mode two ways in — the manual toggle writes [data-theme="dark"], and a dark OS applies unless the user explicitly chose light. CSS cannot share one declaration block between a plain selector and a media query, so the dark palette is duplicated byte for byte. Nothing in the language keeps the two in step; src/ui/tokens.test.ts does. Change one and forget the other and dark mode silently differs depending on how it was switched on — a bug nobody reports, because whoever finds it only ever activates dark one way.

nodes.label: the four loud dark plates sit in a computed luminance window
nodes.rationale: A plate carries two ratios and only one was ever measured: the word on it (SC 1.4.3, 4.5:1) and the plate against the card (SC 1.4.11, 3:1, seeing the chip is a chip). The light plates cleared both by accident; the dark ones cleared only the first — received at 2.03:1, preparing at 1.64:1 — so a filled chip that read as bold enamel in light was a barely-there tint in dark. The four loud plates are lifted into L in [0.1449, 0.1833], where both hold on --bg-card #192227. On --bg-raised #28333A the windows do not overlap at any colour, so a filled chip there is impossible; outline is used instead and filled is counter-dashboard-only by design §7.2. Delivered and cancelled are left quiet by law, and their word carries 9.57:1 and 10.35:1.
nodes.norm_label: the four loud dark plates sit in a computed luminance window

nodes.label: --bar-fill / --bar-on / --bar-edge
nodes.rationale: The persistent bottom CTA bar (design §7.4) is the one surface that must stay a dark plate in BOTH themes, so it gets a role of its own. It used --bg-inverse, which did exactly what 'inverse' promises and turned into a near-white slab across the bottom of a dark phone. In dark it now sits only 1.4:1 above the page, so --bar-edge is not decoration — it is what makes it read as a plate at all.

nodes.label: --scrim
nodes.rationale: One value in both themes. Stock ShadCN uses a 50% black wash, which measures 1.08:1 against the dark app ground — in dark it dimmed nothing and the dialog floated over a page that still looked live. Mixing towards --steel-950, the darkest step in a ramp that does not move, suppresses whatever is actually bright behind a dialog in either theme. Re-pointing it would mean finding something darker than the darkest step, which is why it is the one documented exemption from 'dark re-points every role'.

nodes.label: --text-tertiary is card-only
nodes.rationale: 4.69:1 on --bg-card but 4.13:1 on --bg-app and 3.76:1 on --bg-sunken, both under the 4.5 floor. The only step in the steel ramp that clears every light ground is steel-600, which is already --text-secondary; in dark the only step that clears every ground is steel-300, likewise already --text-secondary. There is no value both universal and distinct from the role above it, so card-only is a property of the role rather than a defect to fix.

nodes.label: --brand-edge removed rather than repaired
nodes.rationale: It read var(--brand-ink), which resolves against :root and is then inherited as an already-resolved string, so a restaurant's [data-brand] block could never change it — frozen at the steel fallback in both themes. Nothing consumed it. Removed rather than repaired, because a token that cannot carry the value its name promises is a trap for whoever reaches for it next.

nodes.label: color-scheme follows the manual choice
nodes.rationale: color-scheme is what the UA draws select popups, scrollbars, checkboxes and date pickers from. Declared once on :root as 'light dark' it means 'page supports both, you choose', so the native layer followed the OS while the palette followed [data-theme] — a cook who set the counter tablet to Light under a dark OS got light panels with dark dropdowns. Two rules pin the native layer to the same choice; :root keeps 'light dark' so that with no manual choice — the customer ordering page, always — the OS still decides.

nodes.label: test: the two dark blocks stay identical
nodes.rationale: The invariant the language cannot express. Two assertions: the blocks define exactly the same token names, and give every token the same value. A token themed under one dark trigger but not the other means dark mode differs depending on whether it came from the toggle or the OS.
nodes.norm_label: test: the two dark blocks stay identical

nodes.label: §13 gate: the word on a filled plate clears 4.5:1 in both themes
nodes.rationale: Design §13 named contrast gates 'to enforce in CI'. Nothing enforced them, and the gap let the dark plates ship at 1.64–2.03:1 against the card they sit on — a filled chip that read as bold enamel in light was a barely-there tint in dark, in both themes' own documented palette. The test is the enforcement the design document only described.
nodes.norm_label: §13 gate: the word on a filled plate clears 4.5:1 in both themes

nodes.label: §13 gate: a filled plate clears 3:1 against its card
nodes.rationale: SC 1.4.11 — seeing that the chip is a chip. Only the four loud states are asserted: delivered and cancelled are exempt by law rather than by oversight, because 'delivered returns to steel' makes them recede on purpose and their word carries 9.57:1 and 10.35:1, which is what identifies them.
nodes.norm_label: §13 gate: a filled plate clears 3:1 against its card

nodes.label: §13 gate: primary and secondary text clear 4.5:1 on every ground
nodes.rationale: A text role is only as good as the ground it lands on, and design §3.1 measured each role once — on the card. Only --text-primary and --text-secondary survive that generalisation, so they are asserted across --bg-app, --bg-card, --bg-raised and --bg-sunken in both themes.
nodes.norm_label: §13 gate: primary and secondary text clear 4.5:1 on every ground

nodes.label: §13 gate: --text-tertiary is card-only
nodes.rationale: Pins the one ground the role is valid on, so the restriction is enforced rather than remembered. The ramp has no room between 'readable anywhere' and 'too light', so the role cannot be widened by choosing a better colour.

nodes.label: §13 gate: the cart bar stays a dark plate with a legible word and a real seam
nodes.rationale: Two-part rule: the word on the bar clears 4.5:1, and if the plate itself is under 3:1 against the page then --bar-edge must exist and supply at least 3:1 against the fill. Light gets its separation from the plate; dark needs the edge, because at 1.4:1 a raised plate is not a plate without one.
nodes.norm_label: §13 gate: the cart bar stays a dark plate with a legible word and a real seam

nodes.label: test: dark re-points every role the light palette defines
nodes.rationale: Catches a role that carries a colour in light but is never re-pointed for dark, so it keeps its light value on a dark background. The exemptions are reasoned, not convenient: the steel ramp is raw material and is the same in both themes (which is why the design doc says not to pair by ramp number); type, space, radius, motion and touch targets are theme-independent by design; --scrim is constant by design; a role that resolves to another role follows it; and --elev-0 is 'none' and has no colour to re-point.
nodes.norm_label: test: dark re-points every role the light palette defines

nodes.label: resolve(): follow a var() chain to a literal colour
nodes.rationale: The dark palette is built as light overlaid with the manual dark block, then var() chains are walked to a hex, so the tests measure what a browser would actually compute rather than what the file literally says.
nodes.norm_label: resolve(): follow a var() chain to a literal colour

nodes.label: STT_PRICES
nodes.rationale: Speech priced by the minute because that is how speech vendors bill. whisper is 0 — on the restaurant's own hardware (ADR 0007), and electricity is not a per-second price because Build Spec §13 bills calls, not watts, the same reasoning as ollama in the LLM table. Sarvam's ₹0.50/minute is UNVERIFIED: no account to confirm it against and no invoice to check it with, and the ledger feeds §12's ₹15 alert, so a wrong price means a bell that never rings. mock is priced at 0 so the loop treats every adapter alike and the ledger path is exercised in mock mode.

nodes.label: ADR 0007 moved speech off the invoice
nodes.rationale: Build Spec §10's cost table budgets speech at roughly a third of a call, assuming Sarvam. ADR 0007 put whisper on the restaurant's own machine instead, where the per-call speech cost is zero and §12's alert has that much more headroom. Worth remembering when Sarvam is switched on: it is not a swap, it is a new line on the invoice.
nodes.norm_label: adr 0007 moved speech off the invoice

nodes.label: Gemini lite-tier prices marked UNVERIFIED
nodes.rationale: ADR 0006 moved the model to the lite tier because a phone call cannot wait for the full Flash models, and the lite prices are below what Build Spec §10's cost table assumed, so the ₹8–20 per call estimate holds with room to spare. The figures are flagged UNVERIFIED at 2026-09-21 because the pricing page was not reachable; re-check at kickoff, and whenever a vendor reprices.

nodes.label: INR_PER_USD and PRICES_AS_OF
nodes.rationale: USD list prices are held in cents so every paise figure is an exact integer, and the rupee rate is one constant so a currency move is a one-line change. PRICES_AS_OF records when the prices were last read off the vendors' pages, because these numbers decide when the §12 alarm rings.

nodes.label: voice trace CLI
nodes.rationale: The eval harness scores the cart at the end of a turn; when the cart is wrong it cannot say whether the assistant misheard the caller or simply ran out of tool rounds before it finished adding. Printing every tool call in order, with its round, its arguments and whether it was refused, distinguishes the two immediately.

nodes.label: the trace uses the eval's caller
nodes.rationale: Consent recorded, no name, no history — the same caller the eval uses, so the greeting cannot steer the turn being measured. Confidence is pinned at 0.95, above Build Spec §5.3's gate, so the trace is never confounded by the low-confidence path.
nodes.norm_label: the trace uses the eval's caller

nodes.label: closeLabel is a prop, not a hard-coded word
nodes.rationale: The product ships English, Hindi and Kannada, so a primitive must not hard-code a word a customer or a cook will read — including one only a screen reader reads. Every caller on a translated surface passes t('common.close'); the English default exists only so an untranslated internal screen still renders.
nodes.norm_label: closelabel is a prop, not a hard-coded word

nodes.label: the close control is a real touch target
nodes.rationale: Not a 70% glyph that fades up to 100% on hover: opacity is not an affordance (§11.10) and a 16px glyph is not a target (§6.1). It carries the density touch floors instead — 44px customer, 56px counter, 32px dense — and disabled is the explicit sunken/disabled pair rather than a fade.
nodes.norm_label: the close control is a real touch target

nodes.label: the chevron is a token colour, not an opacity
nodes.rationale: A faded glyph is a new contrast ratio nobody computed, so the icon takes --text-secondary via text-muted-foreground instead of a 50% opacity.
nodes.norm_label: the chevron is a token colour, not an opacity

nodes.label: the ! on the disabled declarations is load-bearing
nodes.rationale: The checked rules set the same three properties, and Tailwind emits data-* variants after pseudo-class ones at equal specificity. Without the ! a disabled AND checked switch won the cascade with the action fill and read as a live, tappable ON — precisely the state the §11.10 explicit pair exists to make unmistakable. Cascade order, not laziness.
nodes.norm_label: the ! on the disabled declarations is load-bearing

nodes.label: Per-call spend alert at ₹15, guardrail at ₹20 (Build Spec §12)
nodes.rationale: The alert is computed from call_cost, so every price in src/voice/pricing.ts decides when the alarm rings — and a missing or invented one means it never does.

hyperedges.label: Primitive → utility → bridge → token → theme
hyperedges.rationale: A primitive renders Tailwind utilities; shadcn-bridge.css gives each utility a var(--token) via @theme inline; tokens.css re-points that token under [data-theme="dark"] and prefers-color-scheme; so the primitive is correct in both themes with no .dark class, no next-themes and no dark: utility, and it borrows src/ui/Button.tsx rather than shipping a second button. No pairwise edge carries the whole chain.

hyperedges.label: A clip's path: listen route → adapter → confidence gate → cost ledger
hyperedges.rationale: The transport posts multipart audio to listen; the selected adapter returns {text, confidence, seconds, provider, model}; the derived confidence meets Build Spec §5.3's 0.6 gate (null meaning unknown, which the gate must not read as low); the seconds are priced and written to the call ledger's stt_paise and stt_seconds. Transcribing is deliberately a separate failure from answering, so the whole chain runs before /turn is ever called.

hyperedges.label: Why Kannada went 86% → 100%
hyperedges.source_location: ### What was wrong, and what fixed it
hyperedges.rationale: search_menu matches a Latin-script menu and menu_vocabulary is M4, so a Kannada query returns nothing; the assistant compensated by translating and re-searching, which costs one of the four tool rounds a turn allows; because nothing in the prompt named the menu's script it only did that about half the time, so the same case passed one run and failed the next — the variance, not recognition, was the 86%. npm run trace made the round-by-round sequence visible, and two prompt lines (menu is Latin script; batch a multi-dish order) removed the variance to give 100% with zero genuine failures.
